chapters.title: Chapter 5662: How To Kill An Immense One? I
paragraphs: Descartes looked at Noah calmly.
"Do you know what you are, Youngest?"Descartes asked. "Not your titles. Those are decoration. I mean the rare thing. The thing that makes an old creature like me cross a threshold to look at you."
Noah met the deep eyes and said nothing.
"You are one of the few who wants to change the shape of things." Descartes clasped his hands behind his back.

"That is rarer than you would believe. Existence is vast beyond any counting, and it is packed corner to corner with the mighty, and almost none of them want anything more than a larger portion of exactly what already is. A deeper cage. A higher rung. A wider vineyard. They climb and they climb, and not one in a billion ever lifts his head to ask whether the ladder should exist at all."

"And of that one in a billion who does ask, who does look up and hate the ladder and dream of tearing it down, almost every single one lacks the power to so much as scratch it. They rage. They write manifestos in their own blood. They die small, and existence does not so much as pause to note the passing. Vakochev was rare, Youngest. He was one of the ones who both wanted it and nearly had the means. And you already know how that ended."
"He failed," Noah said. "And retreated."
"He failed and retreated." Descartes nodded, unbothered, as though failure were simply a data point and not a tragedy.
"Which brings me to my question. Forget the Scales. Forget the Ruling and the Train and the whole grinding pageant the architects have arranged for us. Set all of it down, and answer me one thing."
The old philosopher’s gaze sharpened to a point.
"How would you kill an Immense One?"
HUUM!

The question landed with weight! It pressed on the concept of the thing, on the sheer blasphemy of the sentence spoken aloud, and Noah felt the subtracted space around them tighten as though existence itself had leaned in to hear.
Noah’s eyes sharpened.
And then he shook his head.
"I don’t have enough information to answer that confidently,"he said."I don’t know."
Descartes smiled, and it was the first warm thing his face had done.
"Good," the philosopher said."A man who claims to know is a man who has stopped thinking. But you should know. So let me give you the information you lack."

"To understand how to kill one of Those Who Remain,"Descartes began, "you must first stop thinking of them as a wall, and start thinking of them as a kind. And to know their kind, you must set them beside the only thing in existence that shares their nature. You must set them beside a Provenance Lifeform."
He began to walk a slow circle in the nothing, hands behind his back, and Noah turned with him.

"They are not so different as the frightened believe. Both generate their own standing. Both owe nothing to any framework. Both are answered by existence rather than answering to it. The difference between an Immense One and a Provenance Lifeform is not a difference of kind. It is only a difference of degree, and of one other thing. But before I name it, for you to truly understand, I would rather tell you a story."
Noah inclined his head. He loved old monsters who talked freely and gave him lots of information!

"Long ago," Descartes said, and the subtracted dark seemed to deepen and settle around the telling, "so long ago that the rulings had not yet been weighed and the architects were young, there walked a company of Provenance Lifeforms. A grand company. They generated their own light, and they wanted for nothing, and they moved through the early dark as sovereigns of themselves, which is the only true sovereignty there is."

"One day, they came upon another of their kind, sitting alone against a stone. He was dying. His light had thinned to almost nothing. His generation had faltered, his essence had begun to scatter, and by every measure the company could take, he had perhaps a handful of years left before he unwove entirely."

"Now, a Provenance Lifeform does not die easily, and does not die often, and to see one of their own kind fading against a stone moved the company deeply. They gathered around him. They offered him their own generation, their own light, the deepest gift one sovereign existence can offer another. They told him they would not let him die. They had the means to arrest his fading, to prop him up, to buy him Ages he could not buy himself."
Descartes paused in his slow circle.
"And the dying one refused."

"He looked up at them, and he told them no. He said that his fading was his own. He said that the shape of his existence had brought him here, to this stone, at this hour, and that this too was part of what he was. To be propped up by another’s light, he said, would be to become a thing that was held together from outside. And he would rather scatter as himself than persist as something borrowed. He wished only to live true to the last, and his death was part of his truth, and he would not trade the truth of his ending for a longer, falser life."
Noah listened without moving!

"The company of Provenance Lifeforms thought this a great shame," Descartes continued."A waste. They were sovereigns, and to them the refusal of help looked like pride hardened into foolishness. They argued with him, and he would not be moved, and at last they did the only thing left to do. They left him food. A store of it, enough for the years he had left, so that whatever he had chosen, he would at least not fade in hunger against his stone."
"And then they moved on. And in the vastness of existence and the length of Ages, they forgot him. As one does. As all things do."

sentences.text: Descartes looked at Noah calmly.
"Do you know what you are, Youngest?"Descartes asked.
"Not your titles.
Those are decoration.
I mean the rare thing.
The thing that makes an old creature like me cross a threshold to look at you."
Noah met the deep eyes and said nothing.
"You are one of the few who wants to change the shape of things." Descartes clasped his hands behind his back.
"That is rarer than you would believe.
Existence is vast beyond any counting, and it is packed corner to corner with the mighty, and almost none of them want anything more than a larger portion of exactly what already is.
A deeper cage.
A higher rung.
A wider vineyard.
They climb and they climb, and not one in a billion ever lifts his head to ask whether the ladder should exist at all."
"And of that one in a billion who does ask, who does look up and hate the ladder and dream of tearing it down, almost every single one lacks the power to so much as scratch it.
They rage.
They write manifestos in their own blood.
They die small, and existence does not so much as pause to note the passing.
Vakochev was rare, Youngest.
He was one of the ones who both wanted it and nearly had the means.
And you already know how that ended."
"He failed," Noah said.
"And retreated."
"He failed and retreated." Descartes nodded, unbothered, as though failure were simply a data point and not a tragedy.
"Which brings me to my question.
Forget the Scales.
Forget the Ruling and the Train and the whole grinding pageant the architects have arranged for us.
Set all of it down, and answer me one thing."
The old philosopher’s gaze sharpened to a point.
"How would you kill an Immense One?"
HUUM!
The question landed with weight!
It pressed on the concept of the thing, on the sheer blasphemy of the sentence spoken aloud, and Noah felt the subtracted space around them tighten as though existence itself had leaned in to hear.
Noah’s eyes sharpened.
And then he shook his head.
"I don’t have enough information to answer that confidently,"he said."I don’t know."
Descartes smiled, and it was the first warm thing his face had done.
"Good," the philosopher said."A man who claims to know is a man who has stopped thinking.
But you should know.
So let me give you the information you lack."
"To understand how to kill one of Those Who Remain,"Descartes began, "you must first stop thinking of them as a wall, and start thinking of them as a kind.
And to know their kind, you must set them beside the only thing in existence that shares their nature.
You must set them beside a Provenance Lifeform."
He began to walk a slow circle in the nothing, hands behind his back, and Noah turned with him.
"They are not so different as the frightened believe.
Both generate their own standing.
Both owe nothing to any framework.
Both are answered by existence rather than answering to it.
The difference between an Immense One and a Provenance Lifeform is not a difference of kind.
It is only a difference of degree, and of one other thing.
But before I name it, for you to truly understand, I would rather tell you a story."
Noah inclined his head.
He loved old monsters who talked freely and gave him lots of information!

"Long ago," Descartes said, and the subtracted dark seemed to deepen and settle around the telling, "so long ago that the rulings had not yet been weighed and the architects were young, there walked a company of Provenance Lifeforms.
A grand company.
They generated their own light, and they wanted for nothing, and they moved through the early dark as sovereigns of themselves, which is the only true sovereignty there is."
"One day, they came upon another of their kind, sitting alone against a stone.
He was dying.
His light had thinned to almost nothing.
His generation had faltered, his essence had begun to scatter, and by every measure the company could take, he had perhaps a handful of years left before he unwove entirely."
"Now, a Provenance Lifeform does not die easily, and does not die often, and to see one of their own kind fading against a stone moved the company deeply.
They gathered around him.
They offered him their own generation, their own light, the deepest gift one sovereign existence can offer another.
They told him they would not let him die.
They had the means to arrest his fading, to prop him up, to buy him Ages he could not buy himself."
Descartes paused in his slow circle.
"And the dying one refused."
"He looked up at them, and he told them no.
He said that his fading was his own.
He said that the shape of his existence had brought him here, to this stone, at this hour, and that this too was part of what he was.
To be propped up by another’s light, he said, would be to become a thing that was held together from outside.
And he would rather scatter as himself than persist as something borrowed.
He wished only to live true to the last, and his death was part of his truth, and he would not trade the truth of his ending for a longer, falser life."
Noah listened without moving!
"The company of Provenance Lifeforms thought this a great shame," Descartes continued."A waste.
They were sovereigns, and to them the refusal of help looked like pride hardened into foolishness.
They argued with him, and he would not be moved, and at last they did the only thing left to do.
They left him food.
A store of it, enough for the years he had left, so that whatever he had chosen, he would at least not fade in hunger against his stone."

And in the vastness of existence and the length of Ages, they forgot him.
As one does.
As all things do."

chapters.title: Chapter 5663: How To Kill An Immense One? II
paragraphs: "Ages passed. The company of Provenance Lifeforms prospered, and grew, and became a lineage, and the lineage spread its light across the early dark. But existence does not let the sovereign prosper unwatched. There came a day when that lineage crossed another company of Provenance Lifeforms, and this second company was not alone. Behind them stood the aura of one of Those Who Remain, an architect who had taken them as its own, and lent them the edge of its immensity."

"It was not a contest as much as it was an extermination. The lineage that had once shown mercy to a dying stranger was driven to the edge of unmaking, cornered, their light guttering, an entire bloodline of sovereign existences about to be scattered into the dark with an Immense One’s weight pressing down to make certain none survived."
Descartes stopped walking.
"And then another aura rose."

"It came out of the deep dark, vast beyond the reckoning of anyone present, and it was the unmistakable, existense-bending weight of a second Immense One. It fell across the doomed lineage and it stood between them and their end, and the enemy company broke and fled, and the architect that had backed them, an Immense One in its own right, took one look at the aura that had risen to oppose it, and it fled as well. It fled, Youngest. One of Those Who Remain looked at what had come to defend a handful of sovereigns, and it chose flight over ruin."

"The lineage was saved. And they looked up at their impossible savior, this Immense One who had scattered their doom, and they waited to see the face of the architect who had chosen, for reasons none of them could fathom, to spend its immensity on their behalf."
Descartes let the silence stretch to its breaking point.
"It was the dying man. The one from the stone. The one they had fed and forgotten Ages before."
BOOM!
The word landed soft and landed heavy, and Noah’s endlessly blue eyes had gone very still!

"He had not died,"Descartes said quietly. "He thanked them. Can you imagine it. An Immense One, a thing that architects now flee, and the first words out of it were thanks, for a store of food left against a stone in a forgotten Age. And the lineage, on their knees before the being that had saved them, asked him the only question that mattered. The question you would have asked. The question I asked, when I first heard this tale. They asked him how. How does a dying sovereign, fading against a stone, refusing all help, become in a few short Ages a thing that Those Who Remain flee from?"
"And he gave them an answer of four words, or near enough, and it is the answer I have carried across every Age since."
Descartes turned to face Noah fully.
"He said: I lived truly. Unfathomably. To exactly who I was. I was true."
BOOM!
The subtracted dark rang with it, and for a long moment neither of them spoke.

Noah understood, now, why the old philosopher unmade Primevals with doubt, why he asked a man to prove his own waking life, why he had raised Noah’s own Trueness simply by making him examine it. It was all one lesson. It had always been one lesson!

An Immense One was not a different kind of thing from a Provenance Lifeform. It was a Provenance Lifeform that had lived so completely, so unfathomably true to the whole of what it was, that existence itself had stopped being able to argue with it. That was the difference of degree. That was the only difference there was. The architects were not born above the sovereign!
They had simply out-truthed the sovereign, across Ages, until their truth became the floor everything else stood upon.
And Descartes watched the understanding move across Noah’s still face, and he nodded, satisfied, and delivered the point of the whole long telling.

"So." The old man’s eyes glittered with a cold, absolute logic. "You asked me how to kill an Immense One, and I told you I could not answer that until we had simplified the equation. Now we have simplified it. An Immense One is only a Provenance Lifeform that has gone all the way. So the question is no longer a blasphemy. It is no longer even a large question. It has become a small one, and a plain one, and I will now ask it of you, since you are the one thing in this room built to answer it."
He leaned in, and the weight of it pressed against the very root of Noah’s existence.
"How does one kill a Provenance Lifeform?"
BOOM!
"Would you be able to tell me that, O Provenance Lifeform?"

The words hung in the subtracted dark, unbearably heavy, and Descartes simply waited, patient as stone, for the being he had crossed a threshold to test to reach for its own throat and describe how the cut was made!
At times, there is a moment in any real question when the person asked stops looking for the clever answer and starts looking at himself.
He wasn’t surprised that this being found out he was a Provenance Lifeform. So he instead thought about what anseer he could give.
Noah did not rush it.
"There are two ways that I’ve thought about," he said finally.
Descartes said nothing. He only waited!

"The first is the obvious one. You cannot out-power a Provenance Lifeform. Not really. Pour enough weight onto one and you flatten the body, but the body was never the thing. A Provenance Lifeform generates itself. It is a well. And you do not kill a well by emptying the bucket, because the bucket fills again from below. So the first way is not to strike the water. It is to strike the source. You have to reach past everything it has made and get your hand around the act of making itself, and you have to convince it, at the root, to stop."
He turned the thought over as he spoke.

"A Provenance Lifeform is a thing that answers to nothing outside itself. That is its glory and its single flaw. Because if nothing outside can command it, then the only thing that can stop its generation is the thing inside. You do not conquer a sovereign. You make the sovereign issue the order against itself. You corrupt the well at its head so that it poisons everything it pours. You get it to doubt its own truth for one full breath, and in that breath, its generation turns on itself, and it unmakes what it was still in the middle of making. It does not die of a wound. It dies of a contradiction. It becomes a thing that is generating and un-generating in the same instant, and it tears itself apart trying to be both."
Descartes’ eyes had gone very still!

chapters.title: Chapter 5664: The Thing Beneath The Fruit! I
paragraphs: "That is the clean way,"Noah said. "The philosopher’s way. You would like it. It is almost bloodless."
"And the second?"
Noah’s endlessly blue eyes cooled.
"The second is not bloodless at all."

"A Provenance Lifeform is true. That is what it is, all the way down, a truth that generates itself and owes nothing. But a truth is only a truth as long as it is whole. So the second way is not to argue with the truth. It is to divide it. You do not try to overpower a sovereign existence and you do not try to trick it into doubt. You get inside the one indivisible thing it is, and you split it into two things that are each almost it, and then you make those two halves true against each other."
His voice stayed level.

"Because a Provenance Lifeform cannot be commanded from outside, but it also cannot survive being two sovereigns in one skin. Set half of its own truth against the other half. Make its generation fight its generation. It will pour its entire infinite wellspring into winning a war against itself, and it will win, and in winning it will have spent everything it was on destroying half of what it was, and what remains will be a sovereign that has already killed the thing it most needed to stay whole. You make it the murderer and the murdered at once, and you simply wait for the survivor to notice it cannot live as half a truth."
The dark was silent.

"One way corrupts the source until it poisons itself,"Noah finished. "The other divides the truth until it wars with itself. Both of them work the same way underneath, if you look. You cannot kill a thing that answers to nothing. So you make it the only authority it will ever obey. You turn the sovereign into its own executioner, and you get out of the way."
Descartes nodded.
"Yes," the old man said simply. "Those are...theories and possibilities, but they are possibilities. Keep them in mind, Youngest. Keep them very close, for what is to come."
He turned his face away, toward nothing, toward the whole grinding architecture of the Train that lay beyond.

"You and I should never have met,"Descartes said. "In all the vastness of existence, the odds of two beings like us occupying the same small Dimension at the same small hour are so thin as to be a joke. We are ants. Rare ants. The kind of ant that might one day look up at the boot and decide to bite. And existence is very large, and it scatters its rare ants very wide, precisely so that they never meet, never talk, never add themselves together into something the boot has to actually fear."
He gestured, one slow hand, at the sealed borders of the rushing Dimension.

"And yet here we are. Because THE Immense Ones have a way of undoing their own precautions. They cannot help themselves. They gathered us. This Train they built, this grand moving pageant of chained Dimensions, they call it a Narrative, and the young ones aboard it believe they have been offered a stage to win glory on. They have not. It is a prison. You and I have been swept into a prison."
Descartes’ voice grew heavier with every word!

"And it is not even a prison, when you look at it plainly. A prison keeps things alive. This is not built to keep. It is grounds of an execution, and we are the condemned who have not yet been told the sentence, marched together down a hallway that only runs one direction."
Noah listened without a word, and his mind was already moving ahead of the old man’s mouth!
"That tree,"Descartes said.
Noah’s gaze had already gone to it.

"Some may think it is a prize. Existence told everyone it is a prize, a Pure Blood Fruit, a ladder to greater Dimensionality, a treasure worth crossing doors and killing for. And it is those things. But that is not why it is here." The philosopher’s eyes glittered.

"It is a lure and it is a net at once. Pure Blood is the blood of the architects. It calls to what is like it. Get near that tree, reach for it, consume it, and the thing wakes and it knows. It knows that something of Immense blood, or something with the audacity to reach for Immense blood, is standing in this Cabin. It is not a fruit. It is a nose. The architects planted a nose in your Dimension to smell whether anything worth executing had washed up in the back of their Train."
"Or so it should have worked,"Descartes murmured."A quiet nose, sniffing for one thing at a time. Except."
He almost smiled.

"Except that I am here. Standing beside you. Two of us, in one small confined space, both of us the exact thing that tree was set to smell. And a nose built to catch a single scent, given two at once, in the same room, does not simply catch them. It grows suspicious. It begins to wonder whether it is being tested, or fooled, or walked into. And even if its suspicion is entirely wrong, even if it decides there is nothing here at all..."
The old philosopher’s calm did not waver, but something in it went very cold.
"I have found, across a great many Ages, that Those Who Remain are thorough. They do not investigate a suspicion. They resolve it."
HUUM!
The words finished, and the dark released them back into the world, and Noah’s gaze was already fixed on the distant tree.
He watched it change, and it had been changing this whole time as it wss supposed to be producing a fruit!

At first it was only the light. The slow ecstatic pulse that had rolled off the crimson canopy stuttered, dimmed, and then went out entirely, as though something had closed a hand around the tree’s heart. The obsidian crimson of the trunk darkened past crimson, past black, into a color that had no honest name, and the canopy began to draw inward.
Then the tree buzzed.
BOOM!
The trunk split, not broken but unfolding, and the blood inside it stood.
Obsidian crimson blood rose up out of the tree and held its own shape in the air, thickening, hardening, gathering into a body that had never been meant to walk.

It climbed on limbs that formed as they climbed. Four of them, vast and jointed wrong, each one ending in a single tapering claw as long as a spear, four spear-claws unfolding from a torso of dark wet crimson that drank the light and gave nothing back.

It rose over the courtyards, and it kept rising, until it stood taller than the mountains, a fiendish crimson thing of obsidian sheen and terrible cold stillness, and along the ridge of its featureless head, nine eyes opened.

Nine flat gold eyes, evenly spaced, each one holding no rage and no hunger and no thought that any living being would recognize, only a cold and total attention. They opened one after another down the length of that awful head, and when the last of them opened, all nine turned, slowly, and looked down at everything in the Dimension at once.
The cold that came off it was a judgment!

Every Veiled Descendant in the courtyards went rigid, and this time Noah’s Sanguine Mark did not fully steady them, because the thing gazing down was not asking for reverence. It was taking a measurement, and being measured by it felt like being read for a sentence.

Noah stood on his ground and looked up at it, and he turned the full weight of THE Protagonist’s Omniscient Regard upon the thing, demanding to know what had just uncoiled out of an Immense One’s bait.
And the Records answered him with almost nothing.
|VERITAS: ???|
|PROVENANCE: ???|
|POTENTIA: ???|
|PONDUS: ???|
Question marks. A wall of them, the way there had been for Rosalia. But beneath the blank attributes, where a name should sit, the Records gave him one thing, and only one after a little while!
|THE Sundered Scion of Sovereign and Immense.|
Noah’s eyes very still.
A Scion. A child!

Not a Provenance Lifeform and not an Immense One, but a thing born where the two had been forced together, the sovereign and the architect bred into one body and one blood, and something in the making had gone wrong, had come out sundered, had come out as this cold nine-eyed abomination that the architects grew on a tree and used as a nose.
They had not planted a fruit in his Dimension.

They had planted their own broken child, and told it to smell the room, and now it had smelled two of the exact thing it was made to find, and nine gold eyes were looking down at a company of the condemned with the cold and total patience of a thing that had been made for exactly this and nothing else.
Descartes, standing at Noah’s side, exhaled softly, and it was almost weary.
As if this old man...was truly tired.
"Ah," the old philosopher said. "There it is. I did tell you they were thorough."

"Or so it should have worked,"Descartes murmured."A quiet nose, sniffing for one thing at a time.
Except."
He almost smiled.
"Except that I am here.
Standing beside you.
Two of us, in one small confined space, both of us the exact thing that tree was set to smell.
And a nose built to catch a single scent, given two at once, in the same room, does not simply catch them.
It grows suspicious.
It begins to wonder whether it is being tested, or fooled, or walked into.
And even if its suspicion is entirely wrong, even if it decides there is nothing here at all..."
The old philosopher’s calm did not waver, but something in it went very cold.
"I have found, across a great many Ages, that Those Who Remain are thorough.
They do not investigate a suspicion.
They resolve it."
HUUM!
The words finished, and the dark released them back into the world, and Noah’s gaze was already fixed on the distant tree.
He watched it change, and it had been changing this whole time as it wss supposed to be producing a fruit!
At first it was only the light.
The slow ecstatic pulse that had rolled off the crimson canopy stuttered, dimmed, and then went out entirely, as though something had closed a hand around the tree’s heart.
The obsidian crimson of the trunk darkened past crimson, past black, into a color that had no honest name, and the canopy began to draw inward.
Then the tree buzzed.
BOOM!
The trunk split, not broken but unfolding, and the blood inside it stood.
Obsidian crimson blood rose up out of the tree and held its own shape in the air, thickening, hardening, gathering into a body that had never been meant to walk.
It climbed on limbs that formed as they climbed.

Four of them, vast and jointed wrong, each one ending in a single tapering claw as long as a spear, four spear-claws unfolding from a torso of dark wet crimson that drank the light and gave nothing back.

It rose over the courtyards, and it kept rising, until it stood taller than the mountains, a fiendish crimson thing of obsidian sheen and terrible cold stillness, and along the ridge of its featureless head, nine eyes opened.
Nine flat gold eyes, evenly spaced, each one holding no rage and no hunger and no thought that any living being would recognize, only a cold and total attention.
They opened one after another down the length of that awful head, and when the last of them opened, all nine turned, slowly, and looked down at everything in the Dimension at once.
The cold that came off it was a judgment!
Every Veiled Descendant in the courtyards went rigid, and this time Noah’s Sanguine Mark did not fully steady them, because the thing gazing down was not asking for reverence.
It was taking a measurement, and being measured by it felt like being read for a sentence.

Noah stood on his ground and looked up at it, and he turned the full weight of THE Protagonist’s Omniscient Regard upon the thing, demanding to know what had just uncoiled out of an Immense One’s bait.
And the Records answered him with almost nothing.
|VERITAS: ???|
|PROVENANCE: ???|
|POTENTIA: ???|
|PONDUS: ???|
Question marks.
A wall of them, the way there had been for Rosalia.
But beneath the blank attributes, where a name should sit, the Records gave him one thing, and only one after a little while!
|THE Sundered Scion of Sovereign and Immense.|
Noah’s eyes very still.
A Scion.
A child!

Not a Provenance Lifeform and not an Immense One, but a thing born where the two had been forced together, the sovereign and the architect bred into one body and one blood, and something in the making had gone wrong, had come out sundered, had come out as this cold nine-eyed abomination that the architects grew on a tree and used as a nose.
They had not planted a fruit in his Dimension.

They had planted their own broken child, and told it to smell the room, and now it had smelled two of the exact thing it was made to find, and nine gold eyes were looking down at a company of the condemned with the cold and total patience of a thing that had been made for exactly this and nothing else.
Descartes, standing at Noah’s side, exhaled softly, and it was almost weary.
As if this old man...was truly tired.
"Ah," the old philosopher said.
"There it is.
I did tell you they were thorough."

chapters.title: Chapter 5665: The Thing Beneath The Fruit! II
paragraphs: Noah stood on the mountains of THE Serenaros, his endlessly blue eyes locked on the colossal, nine-eyed abomination towering above them. THE Sundered Scion of Sovereign and Immense looked down, its flat gold eyes radiating a cold, unyielding judgment!
Then, the terrifying silhouette of the beast began to blur.

Noah narrowed his eyes. THE PRECEPT OF SOLIPSISM normally blinded others to his depth, but this was the exact inverse. The Scion possessed a Dimensionality so unfathomably deep that it was physically slipping out of Noah’s perceptive frameworks. It was descending into an unseen layer of reality that Noah had not yet breached!
Descartes gazed up at the fading horror. The old philosopher clasped his hands behind his back.

"This will be a difficult one,"Descartes said calmly. "The solution will be with the two it wants to kill. Both you and I will have to find what makes this thing tick, and kill it. Those Who Remain act with boundless power, but there are also restrictions. Even in an impossible situation, there is always a chance of survival."
The subtraction of their presence ended. Descartes and Noah instantly became perceivable to the rest of the Dimension once again.
THE Primordial Paradox and THE Living Paradox floated up to them immediately. The two obsidian anomalies did not carry their usual arrogance.
Their heavy gazes were fixed on the sky, and their bodies trembled under a sudden, crushing oppression that demanded they kneel!
Descartes did not look at his students. He kept his eyes on the blurring Scion.

"Stay close to me,"Descartes instructed them. "And under no circumstances are you to be in one state of existence. Be alive and dead. Be here and not. Exist on a continuum of paradox. Should you slip a single fraction, I may not be able to save you."
The command only deepened the gravity of the space.
Noah focused his utmost attention on the blurring sky. His Provenance churned, drawing on the weight of his 200 Decillion Quarks!
At that exact moment, the nine gold eyes of the beast focused entirely on Noah.
His existence rang with deafening alarm bells!
The sheer, concentrated intent of the Scion bypassed the physical air and spoke directly to the conceptual foundation of the Dimension, proclaiming a single certainty over reality itself!
DEATH.
In the next instant, THE Sundered Scion completely disappeared from Noah’s perception.
Noah did not think as he moved on pure, tyrannical instinct!

He raised his left hand, and millions of Sanguine Blood Drops instantly bloomed into existence on his side. They formed an overlapping, impenetrable wall of crimson gold and stellar blue event horizons, designed to eradicate any approaching physical or conceptual force!
A fraction of a nanosecond later, all millions of his Blood Drops simply evaporated.
BOOM!
They were snuffed out completely!
An unseen force bypassed the Sanguine Mana entirely and smashed directly into his raised hand.
Cracks formed.
His glistening flesh fractured! THE Quintessential Provenance Skin broke!
BOOM!
|THE Quintessential Provenance Skin has been truly tested for the first time.|

|Limits identified. Your pristine vessel is strained against lifeforms that exceed 60 Attributes, even though your own attributes are much lower. Nothing below 60 Attributes can effectively harm you.|
|What has hit you this time is a force carrying an unfathomably higher Dimensionality.|
|WATCH OUT!|
Noah absorbed the sheer, concentrated kinetic impact of countless Dimensions.
For the first time since his transformation, his focus broke!

His body was launched backward with impossible violence. He was smashed across the entire length of THE Serenaros, tearing through the rusted mountains and the heavy purple gold clouds as everything on his path turned into dust!
He slammed directly into the outer barrier of THE Dimensional Provenance Train!

The thick, crystallized glass of the border shrieked under his weight. He was inches away from shattering the boundary and being thrown out into the abstract, lethal annihilation of the crossing-dark!
His Provenance seethed violently. A vast sea of Infinite Sanguine Mana bloomed against the glass, acting as a final cushion to arrest his momentum.
Noah stabilized his broken hand and bellowed into the rushing void.
"I AM!"
BOOM!
His 200 Decillion Quarks rang with maddening grandeur. They roared with absolute tyranny, stitching the fractured skin of his hand back together in a wash of stellar blue-gold light!
Noah breathed out in genuine astonishment. A single hit by an enemy he could not even see had nearly cost his newly forged body its life.

This was the raw, unmitigated product of THE Immense Ones. Vakochev had warned those of boundless potential that they would be targeted, and the architects had not sent a messenger. They had sent an executioner!
SKEEE!
A fearsome, metallic cry clapped across the entirety of THE Serenaros Dimension.

The sound carried a horrid, conceptual weight as up in the skies, the massive floating metal cages rattled violently. Every single Inhibited True Lifeform and Primeval One trapped inside those cages with attributes sitting below 10...simply ceased to exist.They turned into puffs of red mist.

Down in the courtyards, the catastrophe spread. Mahishasura and the Veiled Descendants dropped to their knees, bleeding profusely from their eyes and ears. Several of the controlled Descendants lost consciousness entirely and plummeted from the sky!
Noah felt his own existence ring violently against the noise.
|The sound waves of THE Sundered Scion carryTHE Provenance Cause of Existential Terminus.|
|You are immune to its effects due to the propagation of your Teloi across the whole of your matter.|
|Lifeforms without sufficient backing of their existence are extinguished.|
BOOM!
Noah stabilized his footing, his endlessly blue eyes heavy with coldness.

He looked across the gigaparsecs of his Dimension. Countless spots of mist drifted where ancient lifeforms had hovered just a moment before. The scream of the unseen enemy continued to tear the purple gold skies apart!
In the far distance, Descartes stood calmly near the ashen, flickering figures of his two paradoxical students. The old philosopher did not raise a weapon, but his unfathomable eyes hardened.
"To kill senselessly is the crutch of the unimaginative," Descartes stated, his voice slicing cleanly through the deafening screech.
"A sovereign ends what stands in its way. But only a terrified architect murders the audience just to clear the stage."
Descartes raised a single, immaculate hand.

Existence seethed. Billowing clouds of dense, obsidian smoke manifested out of nowhere, wrapping around a specific coordinate in the sky. The paradoxical smoke forced the unseen layers to overlap with the physical world, stripping away the Scion’s concealment and rendering it barely visible again.
But the massive, nine-eyed abomination was not in the sky above the mountain.
Noah felt the air freeze at his back.
The Scion had already crossed the Dimension. Its position was right behind Noah!
Its colossal jaws were opened impossibly wide, and its nine cold gold eyes locked directly onto THE True Human Emperor!
Before the jaws snapped shut, Noah heard a cold, featureless voice echo from the mouth of the abomination.
"Death is human. Be...human."
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5666: Heavy! Heavy! Heavy!!!
paragraphs: A roar was a promise of violence. A spoken word was a promise of comprehension, a signal that the monster understands exactly what it is destroying.
The colossal jaws of THE Sundered Scion closed around Noah!
There was no time to step through the unseen layers. There was no margin to call upon the Weft or fold space. The nine gold eyes locked onto him and simply asserted that his existence was caught.

Noah did not attempt to dodge as he raised both hands, pushing the absolute maximum output of his PONDUS outward, commanding his 200 Decillion Provenance Telos Quarks to hold the line against a creature whose Dimensionality defied the Records!
BOOM!
The collision occurred.
Cracks spiderwebbed across the air. The physical space of THE Serenaros shattered into absolute white static.
Noah’s Quintessential Provenance Skin tore open.

His forearms fractured under a conceptual weight that carried the mass of ten thousand Observable Existences pressing down onto a single point. Crimson gold blood laced with stellar blue light sprayed across the rusted mountains. The agony was instantaneous and absolute, a blinding physical trauma that sought to unravel his Trueness at the root!
He was being chewed by an abomination!
But he did not break.
The moment his blood spilled from malicious foreign authority, hus existence elevated violently in direct proportion to the injury!
The more his pristine flesh tore, the more tyrannical his generation became. His Infinite Sanguine Mana erupted in a blinding crimson tide, forcing the crushing jaws open just a fraction of an inch.
A quiet, devastating voice cut through the violence.
"A beast that lectures on humanity understands neither death nor life."
Descartes stood on the ground far below. The old philosopher did not raise his voice, yet his words bypassed the deafening destruction and struck the conceptual foundation of the Scion.
Descartes applied...Methodological Doubt directly to the beast’s bite.
|THE Continuum Paradox rejects the sensory reality of the jaws.|
|He dictates that the physical extension of the Scion’s teeth cannot be proven true. He doubts the bite.|

Existence was forced to agree with the philosopher. The colossal, obsidian crimson jaws clamping down on Noah suddenly lost their physical density. The crushing kinetic force vanished, turning the teeth into hollow, harmless shadows passing harmlessly through Noah’s body.
Noah dropped from the sky, landing heavily on the ground.
He breathed out, his blood immediately flowing backward to stitch his fractured forearms together. He looked up at the towering abomination.
The Scion did not roar in frustration as it simply adapted.
If its physical bite was denied by philosophy, it would weaponize its architecture!
WAA!
The obsidian crimson flesh of the nine-eyed titan pulsed. For the first time, the absolute darkness of its hide shifted, revealing the anatomy of its making.
Running down the center of its colossal chest, wrapping around its incorrectly jointed limbs, were thick, blindingly bright seams of pure white authority.
THE Argent Loom.
The architects had not birthed this creature naturally. Noah could begin to theorize and see glimpses!
Glimpses of what an Immense One had done!

They had taken the unfathomable blood of an Immense One and forcibly stitched it to the unyielding core of a Provenance Lifeform, using the pristine white threads of the Argent Loom to hold the incompatible truths together.
"Now that...is a contradiction," Descartes announced, his sharp eyes reading the blinding seams. "Two things forced into one skin, held by the strings of its masters. It is not whole."
WAA!
The Scion moved.
Its nine flat gold eyes glowed with a sickening, heavy light, and it unleashed multiple Provenance Causes simultaneously.

A Cause slammed down upon the courtyard, seeking to freeze the kinetic motion of everything below. A Cause followed immediately, painting the air a dull, dead gray that turned everything into drifting ash.
The sheer scale of the bombardment was catastrophic. It was the brute-force extermination tactic of an entity that did not need to aim!
Noah’s endlessly blue eyes turned cold.
Philosophy alone would not endure an endless barrage of raw architect mass. Brute force would only shatter against a Dimensionality that sat completely outside the established frameworks.
Noah needed to change the rules of the engagement.
He reached into his own depth and activated a mantle he had kept completely hidden from many.
|THE Meta-Fictional Protagonist Mantle has been invoked.|
|You assert narrative dominance over the immediate domain.|
Noah raised his healed hand, his Sanguine Mana flaring as he began to write the reality of the battle.
"A monster built by others always carries the flaw of its makers,"Noah declared. "It attacks blindly because it believes its power requires no precision."
|The Trope of theArrogant Goliath is authored.|
|You dictate that the Scion’s overwhelming bombardment lacks focus. Probability bends to enforce the narrative.|

The gray wave of a Provenance Cause tore through the courtyard, annihilating everything in its path. But because Noah had authored the trope into existence, the wave split precisely around him and Descartes and two Paradoxes.
The destruction leveled the mountains behind them, yet left them standing perfectly untouched in a narrow sliver of spared reality!
The Scion tilted its massive head. Its cold gold eyes narrowed.
It recognized the narrative interference. The white seams of THE Argent Loom across its body flared violently, actively combating Noah’s authorial control!
|THE Sundered Scion utilizes THE Argent Loom and multiple unknown Provenance Causes to reassert the literal reality of its power.|
|Narrative Override contested.|
BOOM!
The backlash of the contested narrative struck Noah directly in the chest!
Pain! Shockingly, he felt actual pain as it wss surreal!
He coughed up a mouthful of stellar blood, his ribs fracturing under the impossible strain of arguing with an Immense One’s direct design!
Provenance Causes! Were these the study and product of THE Immense Ones like THE Sleepless Fiend?! Did thid thing Generate its own Causes, or were they false and instilled in it?
Noah only had such a thought as the battle degenerated into a brutal, grueling meat-grinder.
There was no elegance to the exchange. The Scion brought down one of its massive, spear-like claws. Descartes stepped forward, his face pale with exertion, and applied his unique power to the limb.
He forcibly separated the Scion’s intent to strike from the physical matter of the arm, causing the colossal spear-claw to veer wildly off course and impale the ground miles away.
But the Scion simply ripped the limb free, THE Argent Loom stitching the metaphysical tear back together in an instant.
It fired beams of pure, concentrated Loom-light fused with unknown Provenance Causes from its nine eyes.

Noah answered with Sanguine Blood Drops. He manifested millions of event horizons, stacking them into a dense, crimson gold shield. The white beams struck the shield, and the two authorities ground against each other in a deafening, reality-tearing screech!
The heat of the exchange boiled the purple gold clouds above them away completely.
Noah’s arms shook. His skin cracked and healed in a continuous, agonizing loop!
This fight was one of the worst ones as the enemy he faced exceeded him in almost all ways!
The fight pushed his POTENTIA to staggering heights, allowing him to endure impacts that would have instantly erased a Descendant like Mahishasura.
He was bleeding heavily. His crimson gold robes were shredded.

Descartes was faring no better. The old philosopher’s immaculate robes were scorched. Blood dripped from his nose as he continuously weaponized a weaving Noah affirmed as aCogitoto prevent the Scion’s aura of Existential Terminus from snuffing out their lives.
Cogito, meaning I Think! Descartes continued to think to ensure they werent snuffed out as after some time...
"The seams!"Descartes shouted over the roar of the destruction. "The white threads. They are the only thing keeping it from tearing itself apart!"
Noah heard the philosopher. He analyzed the towering abomination through the blood pouring into his eyes.
The bloody way.
To kill a Provenance Lifeform, one must divide its truth and make it the murderer and the murdered at once.

Noah dropped his defensive posture. He allowed a glancing blow from the Scion’s tail to smash into his side, shattering his hip and launching him into the air. He used the violent momentum to carry himself directly toward the colossal chest of the beast.
He ignored the pain. He ignored the alarm bells screaming across his 200 Decillion Quarks.
He extended his right hand, condensing his Infinite Sanguine Mana and the absolute weight of his VERITAS into a single, razor-thin blade of crimson gold light.
He did not aim for the obsidian crimson flesh. He aimed exclusively for the blinding white seams of THE Argent Loom holding the chest together.
|THE Meta-Fictional Protagonist Mantle is pushed to the absolute limit.|
|You author The Trope of the Fatal Flaw.|
|You dictate that the architect’s binding is brittle.|
Noah crashed into the chest of the abomination.
He drove the Sanguine blade directly into the thickest seam of white thread.
"I AM!"Noah roared, unleashing the foundational Letter of his Tongue directly into the wound.
CRACK!
The sound was not loud, but it resonated with a catastrophic finality.
The Sanguine blade severed the primary knot of THE Argent Loom.

The reaction was instantaneous and apocalyptic. Without the white threads forcing compliance completely, the Immense blood and the Sovereign blood within the Scion recognized each other as foreign, incompatible truths.
The abomination shrieked!

It was a sound of pure, unadulterated agony. The Scion stopped attacking Noah and Descartes entirely. Its massive spear-claws reached up, tearing at its own chest as the two conflicting authorities inside its body began to wage a war of mutual annihilation!
Obsidian crimson blood erupted from the severed seam in a geyser that painted the sky.
The Scion staggered backward, its nine eyes rolling wildly as its generation turned on itself. It was destroying half of what it was to save the other half.

Noah fell back toward the courtyard, landing in a ruined heap of shattered metal and rusted ash. He did not bother standing up immediately. He simply lay there, breathing heavily, his Provenance slowly mending his ruined bones.
"Fuck!"
He couldn’t help but curse in pain and frustration as today, he may have very well died!
Descartes walked over to him slowly. The philosopher wiped the blood from his own face, his unfathomable eyes fixed on the shrieking, self-mutilating titan thrashing in the distance.
The beast was not dead. Its Dimensionality was too vast to collapse from a single severed seam. But it was severely wounded, fully occupied with its own internal civil war.
They had taken an impossible executioner sent by the architects, and they had made it bleed.
Noah spat a mouthful of blood onto the rusted ground. He looked up at the old philosopher, his eyes burning with a cold, exhausted tyranny as this old man said...
"We are thinking things, we just have to outhink this ridiculous beast a bit more to ensure its collapse. Ready?"

The architects had not birthed this creature naturally.
Noah could begin to theorize and see glimpses!
Glimpses of what an Immense One had done!

They had taken the unfathomable blood of an Immense One and forcibly stitched it to the unyielding core of a Provenance Lifeform, using the pristine white threads of the Argent Loom to hold the incompatible truths together.
"Now that...is a contradiction," Descartes announced, his sharp eyes reading the blinding seams.
"Two things forced into one skin, held by the strings of its masters.
It is not whole."
WAA!
The Scion moved.
Its nine flat gold eyes glowed with a sickening, heavy light, and it unleashed multiple Provenance Causes simultaneously.
A Cause slammed down upon the courtyard, seeking to freeze the kinetic motion of everything below.
A Cause followed immediately, painting the air a dull, dead gray that turned everything into drifting ash.
The sheer scale of the bombardment was catastrophic.
It was the brute-force extermination tactic of an entity that did not need to aim!
Noah’s endlessly blue eyes turned cold.
Philosophy alone would not endure an endless barrage of raw architect mass.
Brute force would only shatter against a Dimensionality that sat completely outside the established frameworks.
Noah needed to change the rules of the engagement.
He reached into his own depth and activated a mantle he had kept completely hidden from many.
|THE Meta-Fictional Protagonist Mantle has been invoked.|
|You assert narrative dominance over the immediate domain.|
Noah raised his healed hand, his Sanguine Mana flaring as he began to write the reality of the battle.
"A monster built by others always carries the flaw of its makers,"Noah declared.
"It attacks blindly because it believes its power requires no precision."
|The Trope of theArrogant Goliath is authored.|
|You dictate that the Scion’s overwhelming bombardment lacks focus.
Probability bends to enforce the narrative.|
The gray wave of a Provenance Cause tore through the courtyard, annihilating everything in its path.
But because Noah had authored the trope into existence, the wave split precisely around him and Descartes and two Paradoxes.
The destruction leveled the mountains behind them, yet left them standing perfectly untouched in a narrow sliver of spared reality!
The Scion tilted its massive head.
Its cold gold eyes narrowed.
It recognized the narrative interference.
The white seams of THE Argent Loom across its body flared violently, actively combating Noah’s authorial control!
|THE Sundered Scion utilizes THE Argent Loom and multiple unknown Provenance Causes to reassert the literal reality of its power.|
|Narrative Override contested.|
BOOM!
The backlash of the contested narrative struck Noah directly in the chest!
Pain!
Shockingly, he felt actual pain as it wss surreal!
He coughed up a mouthful of stellar blood, his ribs fracturing under the impossible strain of arguing with an Immense One’s direct design!
Provenance Causes!
Were these the study and product of THE Immense Ones like THE Sleepless Fiend?!
Did thid thing Generate its own Causes, or were they false and instilled in it?
Noah only had such a thought as the battle degenerated into a brutal, grueling meat-grinder.
There was no elegance to the exchange.
The Scion brought down one of its massive, spear-like claws.
Descartes stepped forward, his face pale with exertion, and applied his unique power to the limb.
He forcibly separated the Scion’s intent to strike from the physical matter of the arm, causing the colossal spear-claw to veer wildly off course and impale the ground miles away.
But the Scion simply ripped the limb free, THE Argent Loom stitching the metaphysical tear back together in an instant.
It fired beams of pure, concentrated Loom-light fused with unknown Provenance Causes from its nine eyes.
Noah answered with Sanguine Blood Drops.
He manifested millions of event horizons, stacking them into a dense, crimson gold shield.
The white beams struck the shield, and the two authorities ground against each other in a deafening, reality-tearing screech!
The heat of the exchange boiled the purple gold clouds above them away completely.
Noah’s arms shook.
His skin cracked and healed in a continuous, agonizing loop!
This fight was one of the worst ones as the enemy he faced exceeded him in almost all ways!
The fight pushed his POTENTIA to staggering heights, allowing him to endure impacts that would have instantly erased a Descendant like Mahishasura.
He was bleeding heavily.
His crimson gold robes were shredded.
Descartes was faring no better.
The old philosopher’s immaculate robes were scorched.
Blood dripped from his nose as he continuously weaponized a weaving Noah affirmed as aCogitoto prevent the Scion’s aura of Existential Terminus from snuffing out their lives.
Cogito, meaning I Think!
Descartes continued to think to ensure they werent snuffed out as after some time...
"The seams!"Descartes shouted over the roar of the destruction.
"The white threads.
They are the only thing keeping it from tearing itself apart!"
Noah heard the philosopher.
He analyzed the towering abomination through the blood pouring into his eyes.
The bloody way.
To kill a Provenance Lifeform, one must divide its truth and make it the murderer and the murdered at once.
Noah dropped his defensive posture.
He allowed a glancing blow from the Scion’s tail to smash into his side, shattering his hip and launching him into the air.
He used the violent momentum to carry himself directly toward the colossal chest of the beast.
He ignored the pain.
He ignored the alarm bells screaming across his 200 Decillion Quarks.
He extended his right hand, condensing his Infinite Sanguine Mana and the absolute weight of his VERITAS into a single, razor-thin blade of crimson gold light.
He did not aim for the obsidian crimson flesh.
He aimed exclusively for the blinding white seams of THE Argent Loom holding the chest together.
|THE Meta-Fictional Protagonist Mantle is pushed to the absolute limit.|
|You author The Trope of the Fatal Flaw.|
|You dictate that the architect’s binding is brittle.|
Noah crashed into the chest of the abomination.
He drove the Sanguine blade directly into the thickest seam of white thread.
"I AM!"Noah roared, unleashing the foundational Letter of his Tongue directly into the wound.
CRACK!
The sound was not loud, but it resonated with a catastrophic finality.
The Sanguine blade severed the primary knot of THE Argent Loom.
The reaction was instantaneous and apocalyptic.
Without the white threads forcing compliance completely, the Immense blood and the Sovereign blood within the Scion recognized each other as foreign, incompatible truths.
The abomination shrieked!
It was a sound of pure, unadulterated agony.
The Scion stopped attacking Noah and Descartes entirely.
Its massive spear-claws reached up, tearing at its own chest as the two conflicting authorities inside its body began to wage a war of mutual annihilation!
Obsidian crimson blood erupted from the severed seam in a geyser that painted the sky.
The Scion staggered backward, its nine eyes rolling wildly as its generation turned on itself.
It was destroying half of what it was to save the other half.
Noah fell back toward the courtyard, landing in a ruined heap of shattered metal and rusted ash.
He did not bother standing up immediately.
He simply lay there, breathing heavily, his Provenance slowly mending his ruined bones.
"Fuck!"
He couldn’t help but curse in pain and frustration as today, he may have very well died!
Descartes walked over to him slowly.
The philosopher wiped the blood from his own face, his unfathomable eyes fixed on the shrieking, self-mutilating titan thrashing in the distance.
The beast was not dead.
Its Dimensionality was too vast to collapse from a single severed seam.
But it was severely wounded, fully occupied with its own internal civil war.
They had taken an impossible executioner sent by the architects, and they had made it bleed.
Noah spat a mouthful of blood onto the rusted ground.
He looked up at the old philosopher, his eyes burning with a cold, exhausted tyranny as this old man said...
"We are thinking things, we just have to outhink this ridiculous beast a bit more to ensure its collapse.
Ready?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5667: Never Fair!
paragraphs: THE Sundered Scion of Sovereign and Immense did not die from the severed seam. It shrieked, thrashing in the ruined courtyards of THE Serenaros, but it did not collapse. The abomination simply adapted to the tear in its own reality.

It abandoned the elegance of its executioner protocols. It stopped trying to erase Noah and Descartes cleanly. Instead, the Scion wrapped its colossal obsidian crimson body in three unknown Provenance Causes simultaneously, pulling dense, blinding waves of THE Argent Loom directly from the surrounding crossing-dark to act as a physical cast over its broken chest.
It turned itself into a battering ram of pure, unadulterated mass!
In a single nanosecond, THE Sundered Scion attacked forty times.
HUUM!

Noah met the onslaught with his own body. He did not step back. He threw himself directly into the blinding white and obsidian storm, his 200 Decillion Provenance Telos Quarks screaming under the sheer kinetic impact of an entity bred by the architects.
CRACK!
A spear-claw the size of a mountain ridge smashed through Noah’s. The blow shattered his left shoulder, tearing the crimson gold flesh away and exposing the stellar blue-gold marrow beneath.
Noah did not retreat as he weaponized the agony!
He drove his unbroken right fist directly into the Scion’s lower eye, his knuckles wrapped in countless localized event horizons of Sanguine Mana.
The eye burst in a spray of thick, unreadable fluid.
The Scion retaliated instantly, sweeping a Loom-wrapped tail across Noah’s ribs. The impact shattered his ribcage.
Noah spat blood, his endlessly blue eyes burning as he activated his immensity!
|THE Meta-Fictional Protagonist Mantle is invoked.|
|You author The Trope of the Unyielding Bastion.|
|Probability bends. The lethal trajectory of the enemy’s strikes is forced into a predictable rhythm.|
He forced the Scion to fight on his tempo. Descartes stood on the periphery, bleeding, yet the old philosopher never stopped working.

Whenever the Scion raised a limb to deliver a killing blow, Descartes applied Methodological Doubt. He denied the physical reality of the specific joint, causing the colossal arm to stutter and lose its density for a fraction of a second.
Noah exploited every single stutter.

He drove Infinite Sanguine Blood Drops into the joints. He tore away plates of obsidian crimson flesh with his bare hands. He absorbed catastrophic damage, allowing his pristine vessel to be pulverized and restitched in a continuous, grueling loop of destruction and generation!
He grew stronger and stronger through the brutal battle!
Minutes passed.

Against a creature possessing a Dimensionality that defied the Records, a minute of direct physical combat felt like an epoch of uninterrupted torture. The rusted mountains of THE Serenaros were entirely pulverized. The ground was melted into a sea of slag and stellar blue-gold light.
Finally, Noah saw the opening.

Descartes stepped forward, raising both hands, and applied a massive, concentrated burst of The Cogito directly to the Scion’s fractured mind, forcing it to question its own existence for a single, devastating moment.
The beast froze.

Noah launched himself from the sea of slag. He poured the absolute maximum output of his Infinite Sanguine Mana into his right leg, executing a descending strike that carried the localized weight of THE Infiniverse itself.
THE Infiniverse, now holding the weight of Thousands of Observable Existences! Its immensity filled him!
His heel cleaved through the dense white Loom-cast and smashed directly into the top of the Scion’s head.
BOOM...CRACK!

The impact drove the abomination face-first into the ruined ground. The remaining eight gold eyes rolled upward, the cold light within them dimming into nothingness. The massive limbs went entirely slack as Authority and Causes fizzled out as if they could no longer endure!
The sheer, oppressive aura of THE Sundered Scion faded!
Noah dropped to the ground, his chest heaving. He was covered in his own blood, his pristine skin marred by dozens of gory, exposed fractures that were currently knitting themselves back together.
He looked at the fallen beast.
He did not let his guard down as stupidly...
WAA!
A blinding, impossible light erupted from the corpse of the abomination!

The dim gold eyes did not reopen. Instead, the white seams of THE Argent Loom across its body violently multiplied. They tore through the obsidian crimson flesh, rewriting the biological structure of the beast in real-time.
From its massive, ruined back, two colossal, extending wings of pure white Loom-light burst outward!
|A hidden Provenance Cause has been triggered within the vessel of the enemy.|
|THE Cause of the Undying Cycle is active.|
|The architect authored a second life into their executioner. The physical parameters have been reset and elevated.|
The winged Scion rose from the slag, its form now a terrifying, pure horror of white light and obsidian blood.
Noah stared at the prompt, his endlessly blue eyes narrowing into slits. He spat a mouthful of stellar blood onto the ground.
"Are you fucking kidding me? Hey! Come on!"
HUUM!
The winged Scion did not wait for them to recover. It beat its colossal wings once, and the sheer kinetic force of the motion tore a vacuum in the center of the Dimension.
The second phase of the battle was infinitely worse than the first.
The Scion was faster. Its strikes carried the added conceptual weight of the Undying Cycle. Noah and Descartes were pushed to the absolute brink of their existences.

Descartes was forced to abandon his calculated philosophical strikes and simply erect walls of absolute doubt, denying the space between them and the Scion to prevent them from being physically erased. Noah fought with a brutal, unhinged ferocity, his Infinite Sanguine Mana flooding the Dimension until the air itself was a thick, suffocating ocean of crimson gold.
They tore it down piece by piece.

Noah lost his left arm. He regenerated it in a burst of rage and drove his newly formed hand directly through the wing’s joint, snapping the Loom-construct entirely. He was a gory, mutilated butcher, his regal crimson robes reduced to bloody rags, but he refused to yield a single inch of ground.
Another grueling, brutal set of minutes dragged on.

Noah realized that cutting the seams was not enough. To kill this thing permanently, he had to separate the sovereign from the architect entirely. He had to ruin its truth beyond any capacity to heal!
He waited for Descartes to create a window.

The philosopher dropped his hands, allowing the Scion to lunge forward, and applied something familiar now that noah affirmed to beMind-Body Dualismto the creature’s forward momentum, severing its spatial awareness. The beast missed Noah by a fraction of a millimeter.
Noah stepped directly into the Scion’s side.

He reached out with both hands, his fingers digging deep into the ruined, severed chest cavity he had opened in the first phase. He grabbed the thickest clusters of THE Argent Loom in his left hand, and he grabbed the raw, pulsing obsidian crimson flesh of the Immense blood in his right.
He braced his feet against the beast’s ribcage!
He called upon his 200 Decillion Quarks, his PONDUS, his VERITAS, and his absolute Teloi!
"I AM!"
WAA!
Noah pulled his hands apart.
He did not just tear flesh. He physically and conceptually ripped the two halves of the abomination’s existence away from each other!
CRACK!
The sound defied description. It was the noise of a fundamental truth being broken over a knee.
Noah tore the Scion entirely in half!

The white wings and the Loom-weavings shrieked and dissolved into useless, scattered threads of light. The obsidian crimson half collapsed into a dead, rotting pile of inert Primeval matter. The contradiction was resolved. The truth was divided!
BOOM!
Noah was flung backwards like a ragdoll as grand, cascading prompts rushed into Noah’s vision, bathing his ruined, bloody body in the light of an impossible victory!
|You have successfully divided the truth of an architect’s creation.|
|THE Sundered Scion of Sovereign and Immense has been permanently eradicated.|
|A profound act of generation through destruction has occurred. You have survived the direct, unmitigated weight of Those Who Remain, and you have shattered it with your own hands.|
|Your Trueness cannot be argued with.|
|VERITAS: 51|
|PROVENANCE: 49|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 49|
|OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: 75|
His VERITAS tore through the wall of fifty! His other attributes sat heavily at forty-nine, ready to spill over the edge.
Noah dropped the chunks of dead matter from his hands.
He stood in the center of THE Serenaros, his chest heaving, his breath coming in ragged, bloody gasps. He looked around!

The Dimension was torn to absolute waste. There were no courtyards left. The purple gold mountains were gone. The sky was an empty, scarred void. The ground was replaced by a vast, churning sea of his own Infinite Sanguine Mana, littered with the shattered fragments of reality.
He swept his gaze across the ruin.

The millions of Inhibited True Lifeforms were gone, erased by the Scion’s opening scream. The thousands of Veiled Descendants, the Enforcers, and the Wardens he had planned to use to corrupt the Pax were completely eradicated.
There was only one survivor from the army he had claimed.

Far in the distance, kneeling on a floating chunk of rusted metal, was Mahishasura. The Descendant was bleeding from every orifice, his amber gold eyes dull, his pristine coat ruined. He had survived only because his Ordination of THE SHIELD and his depth had allowed him to barely weather the conceptual eradication.
Everyone else was dead.
An army of Descendants, an entire mountain of assets, shredded without even having the chance to strike a single blow.
Noah looked at the lone survivor, and a cold, heavy realization settled and was affirmed as something he already knew into his bones.
Anything apart from him was useless.

He could claim armies. He could weave entire Dimensions into his fold. But when the true weight of existence descended, when the architects actually looked down and sent their tools, numbers meant absolutely nothing. The followers would only ever be ash in the wind.
As a human, even though it could be terribly lonely, one had to always rely on themselves.

Noah looked over at Descartes. The old philosopher was leaning heavily against a shattered pillar, his immaculate robes ruined, his breathing shallow. THE Primordial Paradox and THE Living Paradox were ashen around him in constant paradoxical states.
Descartes had fought brilliantly as his handicap were protecting his disciples too. He was a monster in his own right. It was human to work together, and Noah respected the old man!
But he could never rely on him. He could not rely on Thalia. He could not rely on any others!
The tools of Those Who Remain alone had been enough to almost kill him today. If he wanted to survive all that was coming, he had to become the only variable that mattered.
Because this was existence.
And existence was never fair!

chapters.title: Chapter 5668: Dreamer!
paragraphs: The center of the gigaparsec-wide Dimension was reduced to a churning, ruined sea of crimson gold Sanguine Mana and shattered reality.

Descartes stood at the edge of the destruction. The old philosopher kept his unfathomable gaze fixed on his two disciples. THE Primordial Paradox and Erwin flickered violently, trapped in a constant, agonizing state of paradox.
Descartes fed them his own authority, ensuring they remained simultaneously alive and dead, here and not, refusing to let the residual Provenance Cause of Existential Terminus claim their existences.
Once he stabilized them, Descartes turned and floated over the sea of blood to stop near Noah.
"Existence loves and loathes Those Who Remain for the exact same reason," Descartes said.
"It loves what they can do, and it loathes what they can do. They have free reign to author the epochs, but they also have restrictions. They can succeed, and they can fail. They failed here."
The philosopher looked at the scattered, rotting ash of the Scion.
"What do you think they will do?"
Noah stood amidst the ruin of his own making, his shattered skin still knitting itself together.
"They’ll simply try again," Noah replied calmly.
"Yes," Descartes nodded. "But they are not omniscient. They do not know many things, and they only know some things. If they fully and truly knew about you or I, we might not be alive much longer."
Descartes clasped his hands behind his back, looking up at the shredded, empty sky of the moving Dimensional Cabin.

"But we also cannot remain in the place where one of their tools has died. That will just give them free information when they send others to check. We are lucky none were watching this Dimension directly... or perhaps it is not luck at all. Perhaps it is a part of their restrictions. If they already had one of their cards on the field, existence demands balance. They could not also watch. Even I do not know."
The old man sighed, the weight of countless epochs settling into his shoulders.

"There are many profundities about existence, about Provenance Lifeforms and Those Who Remain, that remain a complete mystery. Vakochev tried to peer through these mysteries and change things. Even someone as grand as him failed. That alone should have told all of us to not even try."
Descartes looked back at Noah, the corners of his eyes crinkling with a sad, ancient warmth.
"But we are thinking beings, and we dream. Oh, we love to dream."
To dream.
To Dream!
HUUM!
Noah felt his entire existence violently buzz!
The words of the old philosopher did not just land in his ears. They struck the very bedrock of his identity like a physical trigger!
His entire existence vibrated with an unfathomable frequency, and it was his Provenance Essence that buzzed the absolute loudest.
To dream!

It was only human to dream. All humans always dreamed. They dreamed of a better life. They dreamed of a better spouse, a better home, a better anything and everything.The capacity to imagine a reality grander than the one they were handed was the defining trait of humanity.
As THE True Human Emperor, was Noah not the grandest dreamer of them all?

He dreamed of coming out on top against monsters who had lived for Ages. He dreamed of surviving and butchering the exact architects that Vakochev had failed against. Even standing in the wreckage of a nearly impossible battle, bleeding from a dozen fresh wounds, he still dared to dream. He still dared to believe.
At the absolute core of his existence, this was who he was.A human who dreamed of a better life.

Dreams almost always remained dreams for the vast majority of existence. But some humans fulfilled them. Noah wanted to be among them. He wanted to succeed against impossible odds, and he wanted to drag his people to the summit with him.
Noah raised his hands.
He looked at his palms, and small, crystalline tears spilled over his eyelashes. He smiled, a genuine, breathtaking expression of pure humanity breaking through his tyrannical composure.
Deep inside his pristine vessel, his forty-nine singularities of Provenance Essence stopped spinning.
They melted.
The forty-nine dense, stellar blue-gold stars dissolved into a blinding, infinite sea of blue-gold light that began to flood and spread across his entire existence!
They had gained a true, generated identity.

From his union with Thalia Vasiliou, he had generated the weavings of THE Provenance of THE Immense Sovereign. That was a borrowed, integrated Provenance with a very specific identity. It allowed him to edit genetic markers and usher in Nova Provenance Elselifeforms.
But his own Provenance Essence had remained blank. It was just Quintessential. It was just Infinite. It had no defined role other than being his.
At this moment, it picked up an identity. It anchored itself to a critical, core human quality.
The quality to dream.
WAA!
Golden blue clouds of raw, conceptual authority erupted from Noah’s skin!

His physical body became completely surrounded by the billowing light. His existence started to become hazy, blurring at the edges as if he were stepping into a reality that had not yet been authored.
Descartes took a sharp step back, his unreadable eyes widening in profound shock.
THE Primordial Paradox and Erwin paused their agonizing flickering, staring at the True Human Emperor with absolute disbelief.
Grand, heavg prompts cascaded down Noah’s vision!
|THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer has attained a level of Maturity.|
|You dream of a better life. You dream of prosperity, and at times, fear drives your dreams. But you are Human, and you are a Dreamer.|
|Your Provenance Essence takes on the identity your existence has selected for it.|
|Capability Unlocked: PROVENANCE DREAMS.|

|At any time of your choosing, you may initiate your Provenance to experience Provenance Dreams. This will form a Provenance Dream Body that can appear anywhere across time and existence as you dream, allowing you to seek out the tools for a better life.|
|A Provenance Dream can last for seconds or for years, but any power, authority, or knowledge you attain within the Dream remains yours even after the Dream has ended.|

|WARNING: This capability narratively approaches weavings similar to extremely unique Provenance Lifeforms and Those Who Remain. Existence loves and loathes such a thing. There may be unknown dangers and restrictions yet to be accounted for.|

|As your Provenance accepts the quality and identity of Dreams, other capabilities are budding as you can exert and utilize your Provenance on your surroundings and on other lifeforms for you to bring forth what you Dream externally in real time. If what you can envision and Dream is grand enough, you could potentially dream your enemies Dead, and existence may just be forced to agree.|
BOOM!
|Much more analysis is being done on your Provenance as details will follow.|
Noah read the prompts as the golden blue clouds swirled around him.

He had just generated a capability that allowed him to project his ambition across time and space. He could dream himself into unfathomable places and time and harvest power without his true body ever taking a single physical step.
He wiped a tear from his cheek, the smile on his face hardening into an expression of unyielding, terrifying resolve.
He wanted to understand his Dream and His Provenance and act upon it!
