chapters.title: Chapter 5669: THE Human Dreamer! I
paragraphs: When an existence fundamentally redefines its own nature, the physical vessel is the last thing to catch up.
The golden blue clouds of raw, conceptual authority billowing from Noah grew infinitely dense. The regal, blood-soaked rags of his crimson gold robes simply burned away into nothingness!
He did not manifest new clothing or armor. He stood in the ruined center of THE Serenaros as a muscular, flawless humanoid figure forged entirely of stellar blue-gold light.
He was technically naked, yet he was clothed entirely in the unbearable brilliance of his own generated Trueness.

Hazy blue-gold clouds wrapped around his limbs and flooded the surrounding air. To the perception of the physical existence, he began to blur. He was becoming imperceivable to the surrounding existence, slipping into a depth of reality that was authored entirely by his own mind!
Descartes stood at the edge of the ruined blood-sea. The old philosopher watched the golden blue clouds expand, his unfathomable eyes analyzing the sheer conceptual weight of the phenomenon.
"It seems you have made a tremendous advancement,"Descartes said quietly. "And found a way."
Noah looked at his own glowing hands.
He found a way?
The phrase felt unbearably small.He had found something so unfathomably grander that the established grammar of even the Verses of Dimensionality he had put up himself could not even contain it.
He felt...fundamentally different. The way his neurons fired, the way his 200 Decillion Provenance Telos Quarks processed reality, and even the way the words left his lips had entirely changed.
When he spoke, he felt like his words were... detached, analytical, and heavily burdened by the sudden ability to observe far too many things.

"A way implies a path that was already there,"Noah stated, his voice resonating with an eerie, echoing absolute that made the surviving space of the Dimension tremble."I did not find a path. I simply...closed my eyes and began to dream."
HUUM!
Noah lowered his hands, looking through the golden blue clouds at the scattered ash of the executioner.
"What is a dream?" Noah asked, his tone entirely filled with a unique passion

"A Dream is a biological organism’s desperate attempt to rearrange a hostile reality. A human closes their eyes and constructs a localized simulation. They dream of warmth when they are freezing. They dream of survival when they are being hunted. They dream of prosperity when they have nothing."
He took a slow step forward, the stellar blue-gold light of his skin illuminating the ruined dark.

"But humans fail to achieve their dreams because existence is rigid. The physical continuum does not care about the electrical impulses of a fragile brain. The dream remains trapped inside the skull. The dreamer wakes, and the world is exactly as cruel as it was when they slept."
Noah turned his endlessly blue, glowing eyes toward Descartes.

"I am no longer trapped in a skull. I am THE Human Dreamer. My thoughts are backed by the weight of Quintessence. By the weight of my Provenance. When I close my eyes and construct a simulation, existence does not ignore me. It is forced to listen. It is forced to obey. And because I can exert this Provenance externally... I can do many more things."
WAA!
A blinding cascade of prompts rushed into his vision, detailing the exact nature of the authority he had just reasoned into existence!
|Capability Unlocked: THE PRECEPT OF THE WAKING DREAM.|
|You may exert THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer upon the physical continuum in real time.|

|By weaponizing your generated standing, you may bring forth what you Dream externally. You impose the localized simulation of your mind directly onto the canvas of reality. If the conceptual weight of your Dream exceeds the True standing of your surroundings, existence is forced to agree with the simulation.|

|At the absolute apex of this authority, if your vision is grand enough, you may potentially Dream your enemies dead. If their existence cannot argue with your Trueness, they will simply cease to be.|
Noah read the details of THE PRECEPT OF THE WAKING DREAM with cold, analytical perfection.
He did not celebrate as he immediately put the authority to the test.
He looked at the empty space above the sea of his own blood.
"Iam looking at THE Sundered Scion," Noah continued, his voice grand and devastatingly calm.
"It is dead. Its components are rotting primeval ash. But in my mind, the white threads of THE Argent Loom are weaving together. The wings are extending. The nine eyes are opening."
As he spoke, he focused the absolute weight of his newly identified Provenance on the empty air.

"Attributes are merely the foundation of the house. They are the stone. They are heavy, and they are real. But a stone does not build a house, and a stone does not execute a king. It requires motion. It requires a hand. Moirai. Mantles. Unique authorities. These are the hands that throw the stone. The Scion was heavier than me. Its basal authority was higher. Yet, it tore itself apart because its truth was fractured. If one holds a truly unique authority, they can ignore the stone entirely. They can make the impossible happen."
He raised his glowing blue-gold hand.
"Like this."
BOOM!
Shining in brilliant blue and gold waves, the space above the blood-sea violently distorted!

The abstract simulation in Noah’s mind was forcibly written over the physical reality of the Dimension! A colossal, winged, nine-eyed abomination materialized out of thin air. It looked exactly like the second transformation of THE Sundered Scion, but it was forged entirely from stellar blue-gold Provenance Essence.

It radiated the exact same horrific, oppressive aura as the original architect’s executioner. By all laws of existence and authority, this was a living nightmare. And Noah had simply dreamed it into being.
|THE PRECEPT OF THE WAKING DREAM is active.|
|You have generated a localized simulation of an unreadable entity.|
|20 Provenance Essence is consumed and held in reserve to sustain the physical manifestation of this Dream.|
Noah activated THE Protagonist’s Omniscient Regard and looked at the thing he had just dreamed.
|THE Sundered Scion of Sovereign and Immense (Dream Construct)|
|VERITAS: 62|
|PROVENANCE: 0|
|POTENTIA: 65|
|PONDUS: 65|

The attributes sat heavily in the sixties. The construct was numerically deeper and stronger than Noah himself. But Noah looked at the staggering numbers and felt absolutely nothing. His own power was no longer merely a collection of attributes. The fact that his identity couldproducea dream of this magnitude made him so much grander than the numbers could ever express.
He analyzed the glowing blue-gold titan hovering obediently before him.
He knew its shape. He knew its weight. But he did not know the exact weavings of the unknown Provenance Causes it had used to heal itself during the battle.
Noah closed his eyes.He dreamed that he knew.
|You are dreaming of variables you do not know.|
|10 Provenance Essence has been temporarily drained.|

|The authority of your Provenance is actively pulling knowledge from all facets of the continuum to fill the gaps in your simulation. The Records of existence are flowing into your Dream to make it true.|
Noah gasped softly.

He felt the sudden, crushing infusion of raw, ancient information pouring directly into his mind. The fundamental weavings of THE Cause of the Undying Cycle and THE Cause of Conceptual Eradication unspooled across his consciousness. Existence was literally handing him the secrets of the architects simply to ensure his dream remained accurate.
He sighed with a profound sense of marvel!
In the distance, THE Primordial Paradox and Erwin stared at the True Human Emperor as if they were looking at a completely foreign, alien entity!
The sheer absurdity of a being manifesting an executioner that was just killed out of thin air shattered their understanding of paradox entirely.
Even Descartes was silent. The old philosopher watched the blue-gold Scion beat its wings, his unreadable eyes perfectly still.
Noah opened his glowing eyes.
"Dreams can make many things possible,"Noah murmured, his voice echoing across the shattered Dimension."I am a human. I possess the capacity to imagine an ending."
He looked at the ruins of THE Serenaros, and then he looked up at the empty sky, his mind reaching far past the physical borders of the Train.
"Could I dream of a billion Descendants dying... and it happens?"Noah asked the quiet dark. "Could I dream of an Immense One dying... and existence simply agrees?"
HUUUM!
Noah asked the heavy question, and the unperceivable fabric of reality trembled in response.
He knew the answer. To force existence to agree to the death of an architect, his Provenance of THE Human Dreamer had to become unfathomably grander. He needed more weight. He needed more depth!

But for the first time since he had stepped into the heavy weavings of Dimensionality, the death of Those Who Remain was no longer a theoretical exercise.It was simply... a dream waiting to be had in time.
And everything would happen...in its own time.

chapters.title: Chapter 5670: THE Human Dreamer! II
paragraphs: Deep within THE Provenance Realm of the First Lifeform, far from the churning ruin of THE Serenaros, a secondary body of Noah Osmont stood upon the verdant blue-gold hills. The transformation that had claimed his main body cascaded perfectly across the connection.

The regal crimson robes burned away into nothingness. The physical vessel reformed. He stood on the grass as a flawless, muscular figure of stellar blue-gold light. Hazy blue-gold clouds drifted off his shoulders, blurring his edges into the surrounding reality!
He was not merely a body. He was a localized simulation of a completely unreadable depth.
And because THE Provenance Realm was an extension of his own generated identity, the Realm itself answered his transformation.
The verdant blue-gold hills inhaled!

The grass blades elongated and shifted into vibrant, physical strands of golden blue dreamscape. The river of light flowing at the base of the hills dissolved its liquid properties, turning into a churning current of materialized possibilities and unwritten timelines. The standing stones dotting the orchards restructured themselves, growing into towering, geometric obelisks of crystallized thought.

Up above, the unmoving stars in the sky of the Realm violently fragmented and split into blinding blue-gold suns, matching the newly melted identity of his Provenance Essences. Hazy, vibrant stellar clouds flooded the horizon, turning the sterile sanctuary into an endless, breathing canvas of his own mind!
Noah raised his hands, observing the glowing blue-gold digits against the backdrop.
He did not feel awe as...awe was a product of encountering something larger than oneself. He was currently observing himself, and he found the mechanics perfectly logical!
He felt unique as if he wanted to study himself and existence...and he wanted to articulate it.
He wanted to affirm and articulate all thst he did as he found his transformation and newly budding nature far too unique!
"I am."
I.
He found this letter of his Osmontian Tongue to best describe how he was constantly feeling something new!
He smiled as he began, hoping he wouldn’t grow annoyed with his own new voice as he affirmed and analyzed this reality...and dream.

"I am standing on the grass," Noah said aloud, his voice devoid of temperature, echoing with a detached, analytical nature."I am observing the fundamental particles of this space. They are waiting for a thought. I am...providing the thought."
WAA!
The space beside him distorted. Because he was THE Human Dreamer, and because he was within his own sovereign Realm, he did not need to follow the rigid protocols of the outside existence.
He dreamed his opposing manifestations awake.
Two identical figures of stellar blue-gold light stepped out of his hazy silhouette.
On his left stood THE Open Hand. Its edges were soft, radiating a quiet, gathering light. On his right stood THE Closed Crown. Its edges were sharp, radiating a dense, tyrannical gravity.
All of them were Noah. All of them perceived the continuum with the exact same terrifying, detached clarity.
"We are isolated," THE Open Hand stated smoothly, looking at the sky. "The environment has been customized. It is the optimal condition for an observation."
"An observation implies we do not already know the outcome,"THE Closed Crown corrected, its voice entirely flat. "We are merely confirming the inevitable result of our own architecture."
Noah looked at the river of materialized possibilities flowing at the base of the hill.

"I am observing... the memory of THE Sundered Scion and breaking down the structure of THE Cause of the Undying Cycle. A Provenance Cause is a rigid machine. It executes a single function without the capacity for variation. It is... a command."
Noah turned his endlessly blue, glowing eyes toward his own chest.

"We do not hold Causes. We hold Teloi. A Telos is not a command. It is an aim. It is the destination of a journey. We have 200 Decillion Provenance Telos Quarks, each carrying a grain of our nine aims."
"A command is finite," THE Open Hand observed.
"An aim is infinite,"THE Closed Crown finished.
Noah raised his right hand.
"I am exerting THE PRECEPT OF THE WAKING DREAM upon our own anatomy and isolating the Telos of Chaos. I am projecting it externally. I am dreaming an aim into a physical law."
HUUM!
I am! I am! I am!
He continued these affirmations as they anchored him to his reality and dreams!
The blue-gold clouds around Noah thickened.
He simply imposed a simulation of absolute Chaos onto the physical dream-grass ten meters away from him.
|You are utilizing THE PRECEPT OF THE WAKING DREAM upon your own Teloi.|
|The Osmontian Provenance Telos of Chaos is given external extension.|
The space ten meters away simply unraveled.

The grass forgot how to be grass. The blades turned into liquid light, then into solid geometric shapes of screaming obsidian, and then into a vacuum of silent white cold. The concepts of gravity, time, and molecular cohesion actively argued with each other within a three-meter radius!
It was a phenomenon far grander than a Provenance Cause. A Cause would have simply destroyed the matter. Noah had forced the matter to fundamentally misunderstand its own existence.
"It is beautiful," THE Open Hand said. "It is the absence of structure."
"It is inefficient," THE Closed Crown countered. "It lacks a ruler. We must impose order upon the anomaly to extract value."
Noah lowered his hand. The localized Chaos simply ceased to exist, returning to perfect blue-gold dream-grass in an instant.
"We extract value by understanding the mechanism," Noah stated."I am now moving on to... analyzing the human condition. I am looking atwhywe dream."
He waved his hand over the grass again.
"Humans dream because the present is insufficient,"Noah continued "They are cold, therefore they dream of fire. They are dying, therefore they dream of immortality. The dream is a symptom of a flaw."
|You are simulating a localized human timeline.|
|2 Provenance Essence is held in reserve.|

Tiny, glowing blue-gold constructs emerged from the soil. They were microscopic simulations of humanity. Noah, THE Open Hand, and THE Closed Crown looked down at them with absolute, terrifying observation.
"They are born,"Noah narrated. "They are looking at the sky. They do not understand the rain. Therefore, they are inventing many things to explain the clouds."
"They seek comfort in subordination,"THE Closed Crown observed coldly.
"They are building a shelter," THE Open Hand noted. "They are attempting to protect their fragile biology as they are cooperating. It is an act of preservation."
Noah watched the simulation accelerate. The constructs built a city of blue-gold light. They waged a microscopic war. They burned the city to ash.

"They build because they believe the structure will outlast them,"Noah said. "It is a comforting fiction. The structure only outlasts them if they conquer the wind that blows it down. They cannot conquer the wind. They are currently dying in the ash."
Noah erased the simulation. The tiny blue-gold ash vanished.
"They are frightened of the dark," Noah concluded."I am also a human. I was frightened of the dark. The difference is that I am currently replacing the dark with myself."
He looked at the two manifestations standing beside him.

"A Provenance Cause enforces a rule upon the board," Noah said. "Our Teloi, when fueled by a Dream, rewrite the board entirely. We do not need to hunt for Causes. We can simply dream our Teloi into fundamental forces. We carry 200 Decillion seeds of customized reality."
"We can dream a Telos of Tyranny to force an Immense One to obey,"THE Closed Crown stated.
"We can dream a Telos of Harvest to claim the authority of an entire Dimension without shedding blood,"THE Open Hand added.
Noah looked up at the dozens of suns in the sky of the Realm.

His perception stretched outward, past the boundaries of the blue-gold hills, connecting instantly with his main body in the ruined sea of THE Serenaros. He felt the exact same detachment across both vessels.
He saw the timeline stretching backward to the moment Vakochev failed, and forward to a moment that had not yet been written.
"I am envisioning an unknown so called Immense One,"Noah said, his voice entirely devoid of fear, anger, or urgency.
"They are sitting on their thrones. They are waiting for the executioner to report. The executioner is dead as they will hear nothing."
The two manifestations dissolved, fading back into the hazy blue-gold clouds surrounding his pristine body.
Noah Osmont stood alone on the hill.

The transformation was absolute. The human who had feared anything was gone.What remained was a thinking thing, clothed in Quintessence, completely unbound by the rigid weavings of a failing universe.
"I am closing the experiment and begin to move on to...something even grander. "Noah said to the quiet air.

chapters.title: Chapter 5671: THE Human Dreamer! III
paragraphs: He turned his attention away from the microscopic simulations and looked up at his own transforming home.
He turned his endlessly blue eyes inward, pulling the Records of his own existence into the empty air.
WAA!
|THE True Human Emperor|
|VERITAS: 59|
|PROVENANCE: 60|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 51|
|OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: 80|
|THE PROVENANCE ESSENCE ECONOMY|
|Total Generated Capacity: 60|
|Currently Consumed: 0|
|Held in Reserve: 20 (Sustaining External Dream Construct)|
|Temporarily Drained: 10 (Knowledge Retrieval)|
|Available for Generation: 30|

He analyzed the numbers without a fraction of pride or disappointment. His attributes had torn through the wall of fifty, his PROVENANCE sitting heavily at sixty. The sheer conceptual weight he carried now ridiculous!
The economy of his new identity was strict, but vast.

"I have thirty Essences available," Noah stated calmly. "To dream a new dream into the present requires a heavy allocation of reserve. To dream an anomaly into the future requires an argument with probability. But to dream into the past... the timeline is already cemented. The resistance of existence should be negligible as I am not changing anything. I cannot change anything. The past is set as what has happened will always happpen."
He lowered his hands.
"I will initiate a Provenance Dream. I will observe...a beginning."

Noah did not cast an art. He simply lay down on the strands of golden blue dreamscape. He closed his glowing eyes, forcing the physical parameters of the secondary vessel to power down as he went to sleep.
HUUM!
The sixty suns above him dimmed.

From the sleeping, glowing chest of the True Human Emperor, a hazy, translucent silhouette stepped outward. It was THE Provenance Dream Body. It carried no physical density, yet it held the absolute weight of his VERITAS.
Noah looked down at his sleeping form, and then he looked away, asserting his destination.
He simply stopped being in the Realm, and started being somewhere else.
BOOM!

Blinding distortions of existence and time rushed past his perception. He bypassed the white threads of THE Argent Loom. He ignored the ticking hands of the Scales. He descended through the unseen layers of the continuum, pushing through the heavy, rigid weavings of a forgotten Age!
The distortion snapped into absolute stillness.
Noah opened his eyes.

"It is the year nineteen ninety-seven,"Noah said, his voice entirely silent to the world around him, heard only by his own mind. "It is eleven fourteen at night as I am standing in a delivery room in City General Hospital. The room smells heavily of iodine, sweat, and biological exertion."
He looked down at his hands. He was wearing faded blue scrubs. He had seamlessly taken on the presence and perception of a male nurse standing in the corner of the room.
Noah looked up.
The room was in a state of controlled chaos. Two doctors and three other nurses rushed around the center bed. Monitors beeped with frantic urgency.
And on the bed, covered in sweat and gripped by absolute physical agony, was his mother.
Amelia Osmont was screaming.
Noah observed the scene with a profound, terrifying detachment...and emotion as he gazed at his mother.

"My father is not here," Noah analyzed, his gaze sweeping the sterile walls. "He is currently several miles away, consuming alcohol in a dimly lit establishment. He is avoiding responsibility. He is missing the only meaningful event he will ever contribute to."
Noah stepped forward, his movements perfectly mimicking the expected routine of a medical assistant.
He looked down at his mother. Her face was pale. Her heart rate was elevated to dangerous levels. The fragility of the human body was on full display.

"She... is composed of carbon, water, and fragile calcium,"Noah mused internally. "A single blow from a something with mana would vaporize her instantly. She possesses no authority. She possesses no Dimensionality. And yet, the exertion she is currently enduring is pushing her physical vessel to its absolute breaking point, all to usher a new life into the cold."
A final, piercing cry echoed through the delivery room!
The doctor moved quickly. The chaotic culmination of biology occurred.
A small, bloody, crying infant was brought into the harsh fluorescent light.
Noah looked at the infant. He looked at himself.

"A human infant that is entirely helpless. It cannot hold up its own head. It cannot regulate its own temperature. It is a biological vulnerability. And yet, this exact configuration of matter will one day tear an executioner of the architects in half. It will author weavings. It will wear the crown of existence."
The nurses cleaned the infant rapidly. Amelia fell back against the pillows, panting, tears streaming down her exhausted face. Her arms reached out, trembling with a desperate, overriding instinct.
The doctor placed the wrapped infant into her arms.
Noah stopped moving. He simply watched.

He watched the raw, unadulterated love wash over Amelia’s face. He saw the pain in her body entirely subordinated by the presence of the child. She held the small bundle against her chest, weeping softly, her fragile human existence anchoring itself entirely to the new life.
It was mundane. It was biologically common.
And it was the most unfathomably true thing Noah had ever witnessed.
WAA!
|You are observing the root of your own humanity.|
|You are bearing witness to the unwritten foundation of a Sovereign.|
|VERITAS: 59|
|VERITAS: 60|
|VERITAS: 61|
His Trueness shot up, climbing simply from the act of understanding his own beginning!
The other nurses stepped back to adjust the monitors.
Noah stepped forward. He reached out with hands that had severed the seams of Immense Ones, and he gently took a fresh cloth to help clean the remaining blood from the infant’s brow.
Time passed as the baby was crying. It had just defecated itself. It was the absolute lowest rung of existence.
Noah changed the diaper with methodical, clinical precision.

"Such a mundane thing," Noah thought, his endless blue eyes locking onto the squalling infant."It defecates. It requires constant maintenance. The human potential is a grand, terrifying contradiction. It begins in the dirt, and it ends on a throne."
Noah finished wrapping the blanket. He looked up, meeting the exhausted, tear-filled eyes of his mother.
He spoke, using the vocal cords of the nurse, projecting a gentle, practiced warmth.
"Have you decided on a name, Ma’am?"Noah asked.
Amelia looked down at the infant. She brushed a thumb across the baby’s soft cheek.
"He is my comfort," Amelia whispered, her voice cracking with emotion. "He is my safety in all my times of need. He is my star. He is my peace."
She looked back up at the nurse, a tired, beautiful smile breaking across her face.
"His name will be... Noah. Noah Osmont."
HUUM!
The room buzzed with a frequency only the True Human Emperor could hear.
Noah nodded slowly. He stepped back, allowing the mother and child to exist in their quiet, perfect sanctuary.
He activated THE Protagonist’s Omniscient Regard. He turned the analytical weight of a Sovereign directly onto the infant version of himself.
|Infant Noah Osmont|
|VERITAS: Blank|
|PROVENANCE: Blank|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: Blank|
Noah stared at the panel.
The stats were entirely blank. The infant was far too weak, far too unformed to hold any measurable values of truth or weight. It was a blank page.
But the POTENTIA was not blank.
Even here, in the sterile light of a hospital room, wrapped in a soiled blanket and completely devoid of authority, his POTENTIA was INFINITE.
Noah stood in the corner of the room, his detached mind accelerating as it processed the sheer magnitude of the paradox.
"Even when I was just born, my potential was infinite," Noah narrated, the hazy blue-gold clouds of his true existence pressing faintly against the edges of the nurse’s body.
He looked at the infant, and the infant seemed to look back, staring blindly into the fluorescent lights.
"Is this a linear progression?" Noah asked himself, "Was my potential always infinite? Did I possess the capacity the moment I took my first breath?"
He tilted his head, his endlessly blue eyes analyzing the flow of time.

"Or is my potential infinite because I am standing here now? Is it infinite because a True Human Emperor has traveled backward across the continuum, observing his own birth, and by the simple act of looking, I have forced existence to overwrite the infant’s future with my present?"
It was the ultimate closed loop.
A human dreamed of a better life. The human achieved the dream. The dreamer then walked backward to ensure the dream was always the only possible outcome.
"Am I...the architect of my own beginning?" Noah asked softly!
The hospital room dissolved into the rapid progression of a cemented timeline.

Noah stood in the hazy, unperceivable form of THE Provenance Dream Body. He did not move through space. He simply allowed time to flow around him, observing the immediate days following his own birth.
He initiated the second cycle of THE Infinite Provenance Baryogenesis.

While his Dream Body observed the past, his true existence was actively refining the 200 Decillion Provenance Telos Quarks that formed his foundation. He took meticulous care. He did not allow the crushing weight of Existence to bleed into the year nineteen ninety-seven.
He contained the pressure entirely within himself, ensuring he did not alter a single atom of the unfolding reality.
"My mother is being discharged,"Noah said calmly, floating beside a rusted sedan in a hospital parking lot.

"It has only been one day. The healthcare infrastructure of this era operates on a framework of financial extortion. She does not have good insurance. Therefore, she is forced to carry her healing body and her newborn child back to a dilapidated apartment alone."
He followed the sedan.
He stood outside the thin, peeling walls of their apartment building. He watched his mother struggle to carry him up three flights of stairs.
Two days later, Erick Osmont returned.

Noah floated outside the apartment window. He observed his father walk through the door, smelling heavily of stale alcohol and cheap smoke. He watched the inevitable collision of two failing human trajectories.
"You missed it," Amelia yelled, her voice heavy with exhaustion and betrayal. "You missed the birth of your own son!"

Erick did not apologize. He deflected and he raised his voice to mask his own inadequacy, throwing his hands up in a dismissive, uncaring gesture before walking into the kitchen to find another drink.
Noah analyzed the exchange without a fraction of anger.
"My father is a coward," Noah mused, his voice echoing only in his own mind. "He cannot bear the weight of his own life, so he avoids it entirely. He simply doesn’t care."
Night fell. The apartment went quiet.
Noah stood in the cramped nursery. He looked down at his infant self sleeping in the small crib.

The door creaked open. Erick Osmont stumbled into the room, holding a half-empty bottle of liquor. The man looked down at the crib as his shoulders shook. Erick fell to his knees, pressing his face against the wooden slats of the crib, and he broke down crying.
Noah observed the tears.
"Humans engage in destructive behavior,"Noah noted, his endlessly blue eyes reflecting the pathetic, weeping form of his father.

"They are unable to stop themselves. They try to change, but they never do. They believe that feeling remorse alters the physics of the damage they cause. They believe that crying makes it okay. It...never does."
The years accelerated.
Noah stood in a small living room, his quarks continuously bearing the weight of THE Infinite Provenance Baryogenesis in the background. The count reached into the trillions.
He watched a toddler version of himself take his first steps. He watched the toddler stumble, fall, and immediately stand back up.
He watched himself speak his very first words.
"I Am... hungry!"the toddler demanded.
I Am!
The first words were I Am!
Noah nodded slowly. The absolute foundation of his Osmontian Tongue was present even before he had the capacity to understand it.
The timeline rushed forward. Noah stood in the corner of a cramped, brightly lit preschool office.

A teacher with a concerned expression sat across from his mother. The toddler Noah sat in the corner of the room, completely ignoring the other children, meticulously stacking wooden blocks into towering, solitary structures.

"He does not talk much," the teacher explained gently. "He prefers to play by himself. He is hyperactive, yet completely withdrawn. We worry his development might be stunted. He is showing early signs of being on the spectrum, Mrs. Osmont. We may need to start him on medications, and I have a pamphlet here..."

Noah analyzed the teacher. She was applying a crude, early-century psychological framework to a vessel that would eventually hold the weight of Dimensions. She was not wrong based on the data she had. She simply lacked the scale to understand what she was looking at.
Amelia’s face hardened. The exhaustion of working night shifts vanished, replaced by an absolute, fierce protective instinct.
"No," Amelia said firmly, standing up and taking her son’s small hand. "He is fine. And I will take care of him."
Noah watched them walk out of the office.
"She defends me against the labels of her own society,"Noah analyzed."It is an illogical defense based entirely on biological devotion. It is profoundly beautiful."
His VERITAS continued to climb. His quarks grew unfathomably dense!
He watched himself enter his teenage years.
He observed his first love. He observed the messy, devastating collapse of his first heartbreak. He watched himself fall in love for a second time.

"Love," Noah stated, floating in the corner of a high school hallway. "It is a collection of human emotions and chemicals. It is a biological imperative designed to ensure the continuation of the species. It is... very unique."
He observed his first time being intimate. He stood in the corner of a dim bedroom, watching the clumsy, nervous exchange of two young humans.
"An exchange of fluids, elevated heart rates, and extreme neurological vulnerability," Noah observed dryly."It is messy. I was incredibly nervous. But it is the mechanism of generation."
The years darkened.
Amelia continued to work brutal night shifts to afford their existence. Erick continued to drink.
Noah stood in the kitchen and watched his father strike his teenage self across the face. The younger Noah staggered backward, his lip splitting open.
Noah did not intervene. He could not intervene.
"He hits me because I do not conform to his shifting moods," Noah said, looking at the blood on his younger self’s chin.
"It is the transfer of kinetic energy from a failing man to a growing one. The strike bruises the flesh. It does not alter my trajectory."
The timeline neared its breaking point.
The year was approaching the emergence of Mana. The apocalypse was arriving. Dungeons were preparing to tear through the fabric of his world.
Noah knew what came next. His father and mother would face their initial deaths in this era, erased by the chaotic arrival of a wider universe, before he would bring his mother back years later.
He could handle watching his mother die.
But he chose not to.

"The emergence of the apocalypse is the emergence of Mana," Noah reasoned, his hazy blue-gold form turning away from the doomed timeline."It is the start of a simple human becoming something more. The beginning is complete. The rest is already recorded."
He looked down at his own translucent hands.

Over the years spent inside this Dream, he had fully completed the second cycle of THE Infinite Provenance Baryogenesis. All 200 Decillion Provenance Telos Quarks had been refined for a second time. They were unfathomably dense. His entire existence buzzed with a terrifying, contained grandeur.
He decided to end the dream.
WAA!
The timeline collapsed into white static.
Deep within THE Provenance Realm of the First Lifeform, the physical body of the True Human Emperor opened its endlessly blue eyes.
The vessel instantly began to vibrate!

All the conceptual gains, all the unbearable weight accumulated over years of observation within the Provenance Dream, were violently dragged back into the present reality and slammed directly into his physical form!
BOOM!
Stellar brilliant waves of blue-gold light erupted from his skin, wrapping around his muscular figure in a blinding, roaring storm! The suns in the sky of the Realm flared with absolute dominance.
Grand, cascading prompts rushed down his vision!
|The first Provenance Dream has concluded.|
|The second cycle of THE Infinite Provenance Baryogenesis has been fully completed across all 200 Decillion Provenance Telos Quarks.|
|Your physical vessel has restructured itself to bear the newly generated weight.|
|You have attained the Second Tier of The Provenance Body.|
|THE PROVENANCE DREAM FRAME is forged!|

|Your physical architecture now exists in a state of localized fluidity. You may shift the density of your vessel between the physical continuum and the abstract layers of your own Dreams, rendering blunt force and lower-Dimensional authorities completely useless against your flesh.|
Noah breathed in the grand, seething power of his new Frame. He pulled his Records.
|THE True Human Emperor|
|VERITAS: 70|
|PROVENANCE: 69|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 69|
|OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: 95|

His attributes were heavy. His PONDUS had skyrocketed from the successful completion of the second Baryogenesis cycle, and his VERITAS had climbed heavily from the deep, undisturbed observation of his own root humanity.
A final prompt chimed quietly in his mind.
|THE PROVENANCE ESSENCE ECONOMY|
|2 Provenance Essence utilized for the previous Dream are currently exhausted.|
|They will remain unusable and out of your reserve for the next 24 hours until their true weight is regenerated.|
Noah took in the cost. It was a negligible price for the attainment of THE PROVENANCE DREAM FRAME and the vast elevation of his standing.
He stood up on the blue-gold grass. The stellar light wrapping around him settled into a calm, pristine hum.
"It was a good dream," Noah said quietly into the empty Realm. "The beginning...is always good to remind ourselves of."

sentences.text: He turned his attention away from the microscopic simulations and looked up at his own transforming home.
He turned his endlessly blue eyes inward, pulling the Records of his own existence into the empty air.
WAA!
|THE True Human Emperor|
|VERITAS: 59|
|PROVENANCE: 60|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 51|
|OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: 80|
|THE PROVENANCE ESSENCE ECONOMY|
|Total Generated Capacity: 60|
|Currently Consumed: 0|
|Held in Reserve: 20 (Sustaining External Dream Construct)|
|Temporarily Drained: 10 (Knowledge Retrieval)|
|Available for Generation: 30|
He analyzed the numbers without a fraction of pride or disappointment.
His attributes had torn through the wall of fifty, his PROVENANCE sitting heavily at sixty.
The sheer conceptual weight he carried now ridiculous!
The economy of his new identity was strict, but vast.
"I have thirty Essences available," Noah stated calmly.
"To dream a new dream into the present requires a heavy allocation of reserve.
To dream an anomaly into the future requires an argument with probability.
But to dream into the past... the timeline is already cemented.
The resistance of existence should be negligible as I am not changing anything.
I cannot change anything.
The past is set as what has happened will always happpen."
He lowered his hands.
"I will initiate a Provenance Dream.
I will observe...a beginning."
Noah did not cast an art.
He simply lay down on the strands of golden blue dreamscape.
He closed his glowing eyes, forcing the physical parameters of the secondary vessel to power down as he went to sleep.
HUUM!
The sixty suns above him dimmed.
From the sleeping, glowing chest of the True Human Emperor, a hazy, translucent silhouette stepped outward.
It was THE Provenance Dream Body.
It carried no physical density, yet it held the absolute weight of his VERITAS.
Noah looked down at his sleeping form, and then he looked away, asserting his destination.
He simply stopped being in the Realm, and started being somewhere else.
BOOM!
Blinding distortions of existence and time rushed past his perception.
He bypassed the white threads of THE Argent Loom.
He ignored the ticking hands of the Scales.
He descended through the unseen layers of the continuum, pushing through the heavy, rigid weavings of a forgotten Age!
The distortion snapped into absolute stillness.
Noah opened his eyes.
"It is the year nineteen ninety-seven,"Noah said, his voice entirely silent to the world around him, heard only by his own mind.
"It is eleven fourteen at night as I am standing in a delivery room in City General Hospital.
The room smells heavily of iodine, sweat, and biological exertion."
He looked down at his hands.
He was wearing faded blue scrubs.
He had seamlessly taken on the presence and perception of a male nurse standing in the corner of the room.
Noah looked up.
The room was in a state of controlled chaos.
Two doctors and three other nurses rushed around the center bed.
Monitors beeped with frantic urgency.
And on the bed, covered in sweat and gripped by absolute physical agony, was his mother.
Amelia Osmont was screaming.
Noah observed the scene with a profound, terrifying detachment...and emotion as he gazed at his mother.
"My father is not here," Noah analyzed, his gaze sweeping the sterile walls.
"He is currently several miles away, consuming alcohol in a dimly lit establishment.
He is avoiding responsibility.
He is missing the only meaningful event he will ever contribute to."
Noah stepped forward, his movements perfectly mimicking the expected routine of a medical assistant.
He looked down at his mother.
Her face was pale.
Her heart rate was elevated to dangerous levels.
The fragility of the human body was on full display.
"She... is composed of carbon, water, and fragile calcium,"Noah mused internally.
"A single blow from a something with mana would vaporize her instantly.
She possesses no authority.
She possesses no Dimensionality.
And yet, the exertion she is currently enduring is pushing her physical vessel to its absolute breaking point, all to usher a new life into the cold."
A final, piercing cry echoed through the delivery room!
The doctor moved quickly.
The chaotic culmination of biology occurred.
A small, bloody, crying infant was brought into the harsh fluorescent light.
Noah looked at the infant.
He looked at himself.
"A human infant that is entirely helpless.
It cannot hold up its own head.
It cannot regulate its own temperature.
It is a biological vulnerability.
And yet, this exact configuration of matter will one day tear an executioner of the architects in half.
It will author weavings.
It will wear the crown of existence."
The nurses cleaned the infant rapidly.
Amelia fell back against the pillows, panting, tears streaming down her exhausted face.
Her arms reached out, trembling with a desperate, overriding instinct.
The doctor placed the wrapped infant into her arms.
Noah stopped moving.
He simply watched.
He watched the raw, unadulterated love wash over Amelia’s face.
He saw the pain in her body entirely subordinated by the presence of the child.
She held the small bundle against her chest, weeping softly, her fragile human existence anchoring itself entirely to the new life.
It was mundane.
It was biologically common.
And it was the most unfathomably true thing Noah had ever witnessed.
WAA!
|You are observing the root of your own humanity.|
|You are bearing witness to the unwritten foundation of a Sovereign.|
|VERITAS: 59|
|VERITAS: 60|
|VERITAS: 61|
His Trueness shot up, climbing simply from the act of understanding his own beginning!
The other nurses stepped back to adjust the monitors.
Noah stepped forward.
He reached out with hands that had severed the seams of Immense Ones, and he gently took a fresh cloth to help clean the remaining blood from the infant’s brow.
Time passed as the baby was crying.
It had just defecated itself.
It was the absolute lowest rung of existence.
Noah changed the diaper with methodical, clinical precision.
"Such a mundane thing," Noah thought, his endless blue eyes locking onto the squalling infant."It defecates.
It requires constant maintenance.
The human potential is a grand, terrifying contradiction.
It begins in the dirt, and it ends on a throne."
Noah finished wrapping the blanket.
He looked up, meeting the exhausted, tear-filled eyes of his mother.
He spoke, using the vocal cords of the nurse, projecting a gentle, practiced warmth.
"Have you decided on a name, Ma’am?"Noah asked.
Amelia looked down at the infant.
She brushed a thumb across the baby’s soft cheek.
"He is my comfort," Amelia whispered, her voice cracking with emotion.
"He is my safety in all my times of need.
He is my star.
He is my peace."
She looked back up at the nurse, a tired, beautiful smile breaking across her face.
"His name will be...
Noah.
Noah Osmont."
HUUM!
The room buzzed with a frequency only the True Human Emperor could hear.
Noah nodded slowly.
He stepped back, allowing the mother and child to exist in their quiet, perfect sanctuary.
He activated THE Protagonist’s Omniscient Regard.
He turned the analytical weight of a Sovereign directly onto the infant version of himself.
|Infant Noah Osmont|
|VERITAS: Blank|
|PROVENANCE: Blank|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: Blank|
Noah stared at the panel.
The stats were entirely blank.
The infant was far too weak, far too unformed to hold any measurable values of truth or weight.
It was a blank page.
But the POTENTIA was not blank.
Even here, in the sterile light of a hospital room, wrapped in a soiled blanket and completely devoid of authority, his POTENTIA was INFINITE.
Noah stood in the corner of the room, his detached mind accelerating as it processed the sheer magnitude of the paradox.
"Even when I was just born, my potential was infinite," Noah narrated, the hazy blue-gold clouds of his true existence pressing faintly against the edges of the nurse’s body.
He looked at the infant, and the infant seemed to look back, staring blindly into the fluorescent lights.
"Is this a linear progression?" Noah asked himself, "Was my potential always infinite?
Did I possess the capacity the moment I took my first breath?"
He tilted his head, his endlessly blue eyes analyzing the flow of time.
"Or is my potential infinite because I am standing here now?

Is it infinite because a True Human Emperor has traveled backward across the continuum, observing his own birth, and by the simple act of looking, I have forced existence to overwrite the infant’s future with my present?"
It was the ultimate closed loop.
A human dreamed of a better life.
The human achieved the dream.
The dreamer then walked backward to ensure the dream was always the only possible outcome.
"Am I...the architect of my own beginning?" Noah asked softly!
The hospital room dissolved into the rapid progression of a cemented timeline.
Noah stood in the hazy, unperceivable form of THE Provenance Dream Body.
He did not move through space.
He simply allowed time to flow around him, observing the immediate days following his own birth.
He initiated the second cycle of THE Infinite Provenance Baryogenesis.
While his Dream Body observed the past, his true existence was actively refining the 200 Decillion Provenance Telos Quarks that formed his foundation.
He took meticulous care.
He did not allow the crushing weight of Existence to bleed into the year nineteen ninety-seven.
He contained the pressure entirely within himself, ensuring he did not alter a single atom of the unfolding reality.
"My mother is being discharged,"Noah said calmly, floating beside a rusted sedan in a hospital parking lot.
"It has only been one day.
The healthcare infrastructure of this era operates on a framework of financial extortion.
She does not have good insurance.
Therefore, she is forced to carry her healing body and her newborn child back to a dilapidated apartment alone."
He followed the sedan.
He stood outside the thin, peeling walls of their apartment building.
He watched his mother struggle to carry him up three flights of stairs.
Two days later, Erick Osmont returned.
Noah floated outside the apartment window.
He observed his father walk through the door, smelling heavily of stale alcohol and cheap smoke.
He watched the inevitable collision of two failing human trajectories.
"You missed it," Amelia yelled, her voice heavy with exhaustion and betrayal.
"You missed the birth of your own son!"
Erick did not apologize.
He deflected and he raised his voice to mask his own inadequacy, throwing his hands up in a dismissive, uncaring gesture before walking into the kitchen to find another drink.
Noah analyzed the exchange without a fraction of anger.
"My father is a coward," Noah mused, his voice echoing only in his own mind.
"He cannot bear the weight of his own life, so he avoids it entirely.
He simply doesn’t care."
Night fell.
The apartment went quiet.
Noah stood in the cramped nursery.
He looked down at his infant self sleeping in the small crib.
The door creaked open.
Erick Osmont stumbled into the room, holding a half-empty bottle of liquor.
The man looked down at the crib as his shoulders shook.
Erick fell to his knees, pressing his face against the wooden slats of the crib, and he broke down crying.
Noah observed the tears.
"Humans engage in destructive behavior,"Noah noted, his endlessly blue eyes reflecting the pathetic, weeping form of his father.
"They are unable to stop themselves.
They try to change, but they never do.
They believe that feeling remorse alters the physics of the damage they cause.
They believe that crying makes it okay.
It...never does."
The years accelerated.
Noah stood in a small living room, his quarks continuously bearing the weight of THE Infinite Provenance Baryogenesis in the background.
The count reached into the trillions.
He watched a toddler version of himself take his first steps.
He watched the toddler stumble, fall, and immediately stand back up.
He watched himself speak his very first words.
"I Am... hungry!"the toddler demanded.
I Am!
The first words were I Am!
Noah nodded slowly.
The absolute foundation of his Osmontian Tongue was present even before he had the capacity to understand it.
The timeline rushed forward.
Noah stood in the corner of a cramped, brightly lit preschool office.
A teacher with a concerned expression sat across from his mother.
The toddler Noah sat in the corner of the room, completely ignoring the other children, meticulously stacking wooden blocks into towering, solitary structures.
"He does not talk much," the teacher explained gently.
"He prefers to play by himself.
He is hyperactive, yet completely withdrawn.
We worry his development might be stunted.
He is showing early signs of being on the spectrum, Mrs.
Osmont.
We may need to start him on medications, and I have a pamphlet here..."
Noah analyzed the teacher.
She was applying a crude, early-century psychological framework to a vessel that would eventually hold the weight of Dimensions.
She was not wrong based on the data she had.
She simply lacked the scale to understand what she was looking at.
Amelia’s face hardened.
The exhaustion of working night shifts vanished, replaced by an absolute, fierce protective instinct.
"No," Amelia said firmly, standing up and taking her son’s small hand.
"He is fine.
And I will take care of him."
Noah watched them walk out of the office.
"She defends me against the labels of her own society,"Noah analyzed."It is an illogical defense based entirely on biological devotion.
It is profoundly beautiful."
His VERITAS continued to climb.
His quarks grew unfathomably dense!
He watched himself enter his teenage years.
He observed his first love.
He observed the messy, devastating collapse of his first heartbreak.
He watched himself fall in love for a second time.
"Love," Noah stated, floating in the corner of a high school hallway.
"It is a collection of human emotions and chemicals.
It is a biological imperative designed to ensure the continuation of the species.
It is... very unique."
He observed his first time being intimate.
He stood in the corner of a dim bedroom, watching the clumsy, nervous exchange of two young humans.
"An exchange of fluids, elevated heart rates, and extreme neurological vulnerability," Noah observed dryly."It is messy.
I was incredibly nervous.
But it is the mechanism of generation."
The years darkened.
Amelia continued to work brutal night shifts to afford their existence.
Erick continued to drink.
Noah stood in the kitchen and watched his father strike his teenage self across the face.
The younger Noah staggered backward, his lip splitting open.
Noah did not intervene.
He could not intervene.
"He hits me because I do not conform to his shifting moods," Noah said, looking at the blood on his younger self’s chin.
"It is the transfer of kinetic energy from a failing man to a growing one.
The strike bruises the flesh.
It does not alter my trajectory."
The timeline neared its breaking point.
The year was approaching the emergence of Mana.
The apocalypse was arriving.
Dungeons were preparing to tear through the fabric of his world.
Noah knew what came next.
His father and mother would face their initial deaths in this era, erased by the chaotic arrival of a wider universe, before he would bring his mother back years later.
He could handle watching his mother die.
But he chose not to.
"The emergence of the apocalypse is the emergence of Mana," Noah reasoned, his hazy blue-gold form turning away from the doomed timeline."It is the start of a simple human becoming something more.
The beginning is complete.
The rest is already recorded."
He looked down at his own translucent hands.
Over the years spent inside this Dream, he had fully completed the second cycle of THE Infinite Provenance Baryogenesis.
All 200 Decillion Provenance Telos Quarks had been refined for a second time.
They were unfathomably dense.
His entire existence buzzed with a terrifying, contained grandeur.
He decided to end the dream.
WAA!
The timeline collapsed into white static.
Deep within THE Provenance Realm of the First Lifeform, the physical body of the True Human Emperor opened its endlessly blue eyes.
The vessel instantly began to vibrate!

All the conceptual gains, all the unbearable weight accumulated over years of observation within the Provenance Dream, were violently dragged back into the present reality and slammed directly into his physical form!
BOOM!
Stellar brilliant waves of blue-gold light erupted from his skin, wrapping around his muscular figure in a blinding, roaring storm!
The suns in the sky of the Realm flared with absolute dominance.
Grand, cascading prompts rushed down his vision!
|The first Provenance Dream has concluded.|
|The second cycle of THE Infinite Provenance Baryogenesis has been fully completed across all 200 Decillion Provenance Telos Quarks.|
|Your physical vessel has restructured itself to bear the newly generated weight.|
|You have attained the Second Tier of The Provenance Body.|
|THE PROVENANCE DREAM FRAME is forged!|
|Your physical architecture now exists in a state of localized fluidity.

You may shift the density of your vessel between the physical continuum and the abstract layers of your own Dreams, rendering blunt force and lower-Dimensional authorities completely useless against your flesh.|
Noah breathed in the grand, seething power of his new Frame.
He pulled his Records.
|THE True Human Emperor|
|VERITAS: 70|
|PROVENANCE: 69|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 69|
|OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: 95|
His attributes were heavy.
His PONDUS had skyrocketed from the successful completion of the second Baryogenesis cycle, and his VERITAS had climbed heavily from the deep, undisturbed observation of his own root humanity.
A final prompt chimed quietly in his mind.
|THE PROVENANCE ESSENCE ECONOMY|
|2 Provenance Essence utilized for the previous Dream are currently exhausted.|
|They will remain unusable and out of your reserve for the next 24 hours until their true weight is regenerated.|
Noah took in the cost.
It was a negligible price for the attainment of THE PROVENANCE DREAM FRAME and the vast elevation of his standing.
He stood up on the blue-gold grass.
The stellar light wrapping around him settled into a calm, pristine hum.
"It was a good dream," Noah said quietly into the empty Realm.
"The beginning...is always good to remind ourselves of."

chapters.title: Chapter 5672: THE Human Dreamer! IV
paragraphs: Noah stood in the center of his customized reality as he took a slow, deliberate breath. The physical lungs of his stellar blue-gold vessel expanded and contracted, drawing in the heavy, unwritten possibilities of the Realm.
He analyzed his own internal state.
He was human at his core. He possessed the biological and neurological framework of his species. He still felt the chemical imperatives of love, fear, and lust. They were present in his pathways!
But the scale of his perception had fundamentally altered how he experienced them.

He was skeptical of his own emotions. He knew he could feel them, but he questioned if they held the same density as before. Fear was a survival mechanism designed to keep a fragile organism away from predators.But when the organism could simply dream the predator out of existence, fear lost its evolutionary purpose.
Love was a tether to ensure reproduction and social cohesion. But when a single mind could construct and deconstruct Dimensions, the tether felt infinitely thin.
He was a human observing his own humanity from a tremendous, Quintessential altitude.
He sensed the unfathomable depth of his power resting perfectly still within him.
"Ruination," Noah called out. "Infiniverse."
WAA!
The space before him distorted instantly.
Two figures materialized on the blue-gold grass. Because they were intricately bound to his existence, the violent restructuring of his identity cascaded directly into their physical vessels.

They did not wear the ornate armor or flowing dresses of their previous iterations. They stood before him entirely transformed. Hazy, stellar blue-gold waves of raw dreams surrounded them, acting as their only coverings. The waves of energy and authority wrapped around their curves and limbs, blurring their edges into the surrounding atmosphere exactly like his own.
Noah analyzed the extension of THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer.

"My authority is extending to you,"He observed, his endlessly blue eyes scanning their newly forged dream-frames. "It is transforming your baseline architecture. What is the biggest change you can now sense?"
THE Infiniverse looked at her own glowing blue-gold hands. Her expression remained serious and fiercely efficient.

"Master," THE Infiniverse reported."The vast architecture of my body has been growing and expanding rapidly. This is accelerating as we perform more Hearthshifts and become the source for an increasing number of lifeforms. But right now, the primary change is conceptual. I feel like an infinite number of possibilities can bloom. I feel like I could pull from your power and simply..."
She trailed off, her analytical mind struggling to quantify the sheer scale of the potential.
Noah did not ask her to finish the sentence. He raised his glowing hand.
He isolated a single unit from his Held Reserve. He waved his hand, and a dense, blinding sphere of stellar blue-gold Provenance Essence drifted smoothly toward THE Infiniverse.
"Take it,"Noah instructed calmly.
THE Infiniverse reached out. The blue-gold sphere sank seamlessly into her chest.
She closed her eyes. She did not calculate as ahe simply began to dream!
HUUM!

The localized space of the Realm began to vibrate violently. THE Infiniverse opened her eyes, and the sheer conceptual weight of her borrowed dream bypassed the unwritten canvas of the environment and manifested externally.
Above them, the sky fractured. A massive, swirling hypercube of deep blue-white light bloomed into existence and began transforming into an Observable Existence!
The heavy, unyielding gravitational pull of a newly born Existence pressed down upon the grass.
She had dreamed the emergence of a complete Observable Existence!
|THE Infiniverse has successfully utilized a borrowed unit of Provenance Essence.|
|A localized dream has been given physical density.|
|An Observable Existence has been generated and nested within her architecture.|
Noah looked at the prompts and nodded slowly. The mechanics were sound!
"Many more things are possible for us," Noah stated.

"But arriving at this point does not mean we can be lax. It does not grant us permission to rest. Even an authority as grand as this is only ever approaching the type of power that Immense Ones and Provenance Lifeforms have already grasped."
He lowered his hand, his endless blue eyes locking onto the two women.

"We are still young. We are still weak, and we do not know everything. Across the vastness of the continuum, the percentage of reality that a dolphin is aware of, and the percentage that we are aware of, may be statistically the exact same. The expanse is simply that large."
He took a slow step forward.

"Arriving here makes me feel that the mysteries of existence are far too vast and unfathomable. We are a tiny thing in this expanse. Provenance Lifeforms and Immense Ones are just a little bit ahead. We must be careful. But we hold the potential."
Noah looked up at the newly formed Observable Existence drifting against the backdrop of brilliance like a miniaturized moon.

"I am expectant of the future. I am excited for the future. I am fearful of the future,"Noah analyzed, listing the emotions as data points. "This is human. But I can dream of a future others cannot even begin to imagine. We can dream of something unbelievable, and we can force it to become our reality. Let us do it steadily, and not stumble too much. Okay?"
The words were spoken with a terrifying, crushing calmness.
Ruination and THE Infiniverse immediately moved to drop to their knees. The sheer weight of his logic and his authority demanded absolute subordination!
Noah stepped forward and caught them both before their knees could touch the grass.
He did not let them pull away as he pulled them forward, wrapping his glowing arms around their shoulders, drawing them into a deep, physical embrace.
They froze for a fraction of a second, and then they slowly placed their heads against his stellar blue-gold chest.
"You are the only two existences so intricately connected to me," Noah said quietly, his chin resting near the top of Ruination’s hazy blue-gold hair.

"You can feel my changes and my complexity the most. You can understand me when no others can. My mother is not able to understand me like you can. Nor can my son, or my daughter, or any of the others."
He held them firmly against the quiet hum of his generated Trueness.
"The two of you have access to my very mind. Please, never attempt to bow toward me again, okay?"
Ruination and THE Infiniverse lifted their heads slightly. They looked at each other across his chest.

The hazy blue-gold energy surrounding their eyes began to evaporate, condensing into physical, crystalline tears that ran down their glowing cheeks. They smiled, a fierce and absolute devotion radiating from their core architecture, and they hugged THE True Human Emperor tighter!

chapters.title: Chapter 5673: Movement I
paragraphs: The physical embrace concluded!

Noah analyzed the crystalline tears evaporating from the cheeks of THE Infiniverse and Ruination. They were expressions of absolute devotion, a biological and conceptual byproduct of the deep integration between his Provenance and their architecture.
He stepped back as the hazy blue-gold clouds of his Provenance Dream Frame drifted smoothly around his shoulders.
"There is a lot to be done,"Noah stated.
"Now, we must resume the extraction of value. Infiniverse. Ruination. Proceed in pulling the markers of the Laestrygonians that were extinguished by THE Sleepless Fiend."
Ruination wiped her glowing eyes, her demeanor instantly shifting back to sharp efficiency.
"Understood, Master," Ruination replied, her voice steady. "We are isolating the remaining markers for their Causes."
Noah processed the variables of the puzzle. THE Sleepless Fiend was an architect. We know THE Immense Ones play with Provenance Causes, treating them as foundational building blocks.
So why kill Laestrygonians specifically for their Causes?
An Immense One generates its own unfathomable standing. It does not need to scavenge lower authorities. Therefore, the harvest was not for personal power. It was for raw material.

A predator did not harvest wool to become a sheep. It harvested wool to weave a coat. The architects were using the Causes of the Laestrygonians to build or replace something massive. Perhaps it was the very infrastructure of THE Sundered Scions or something like them, or the white threads of THE Argent Loom? He had no idea.
WAA!
Noah pushed the calculation aside, turning his focus inward to test the absolute limits of THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer.
He pulled up the weavings of his Provenance Essence Economy.
|THE PROVENANCE ESSENCE ECONOMY|
|Total Generated Capacity: 69|
|Currently Consumed: 2 (24-hour regeneration cycle active)|
|Held in Reserve: 20 (Sustaining External Dream Construct)|
|Temporarily Drained: 10 (Knowledge Retrieval)|
|Available for Generation: 37|

"The cost...is the friction of reality," Noah narrated, his endlessly blue eyes analyzing the blue-gold grass. "To dream something into the present requires a sustained reserve. To dream and pull knowledge drains the essence temporarily until the data is fully assimilated. But a consumed essence is exhausted entirely."
He ran the simulation of his own limits.
The two consumed Essences were dead weight in his panel. They would remain unusable for precisely twenty-four hours until their True weight regenerated.

This was the limitation of the engine. The authority of THE PRECEPT OF THE WAKING DREAM was absolute, but the fuel was finite. If he attempted to dream an Immense One dead in this exact moment, the conceptual weight of erasing an architect would easily exceed his available thirty-seven Essences.
The Dream would fail not because it was impossible, but because he lacked the capacity to process the execution.
He needed to expand his capacity. He needed to understand the exact anatomy of a genuine Provenance Lifeform!
His mind immediately moved to Thalia.
He considered the Vasiliou Elseworld.

If an Immense One was simply a Provenance Lifeform that had lived so truly that existence could no longer argue with it, then what was the Vasiliou lineage? What could he learn from seeing an entire Elseworld populated by more Provenance Lifeforms?

He analyzed their relationship with Those Who Remain. The Vasiliou hid in an Elseworld. They operated in the shadows, avoiding the direct gaze of the architects. They were sovereign, yet they were cautious. By observing their anatomy and their society, Noah knew he could isolate the exact threshold where a sovereign either capitulated or ascended to become an Immense One. Thalia could be one of the keys to unlocking the true potential of his own Provenance.
He juggled the pieces of the macroscopic board in his mind.
His clones were stationed across the Dimensions. He possessed a vast reservoir of Infinite Sanguine Mana to fuel his Sanguine manifestations.
The entire structure of THE Dimensional Provenance Train was rushing forward through the crossing-dark, carrying its cargo of condemned Dimensions toward an unknown terminus.
"I must optimize the next allocation," Noah mused aloud.
"I have thirty-seven Essences available. The next Provenance Dream must yield a strategic advantage that outweighs the twenty-four-hour cooldown."
Should he dream his way into the highest archives of the Pax? Should he dream himself into the Vasiliou Elseworld to observe their sovereign generation undetected? Could he?
Or should he look directly at the higher Dimensions of the Train? Or something else entirely?
He looked at THE Infiniverse, who was currently analyzing the newly born Observable Existence she had just dreamed into reality.
"We will continue the harvest," Noah commanded.
"Continue with the extraction the Laestrygonian markers. Map the trajectory of THE Sleepless Fiend’s actions. And continue the Hearthshifts. I will dream again very soon."
HUUM!

The sixty-nine suns above them flared with quiet, unyielding tyranny. Noah stood in the center of his customized reality, perfectly still, calculating the exact cost of overwriting the rest of existence!
His vision refocused and recalibrated.
The physical continuum of THE Serenaros Dimension remained a ruined canvas.

Noah stood in the center of the churning sea of his own Infinite Sanguine Mana. His primary vessel processed the exact same sensory data and conceptual weight as the secondary vessel resting within his Realm. The connection was seamless.
He turned his endlessly blue, glowing eyes away from the scattered ash of the executioner and looked toward the edge of the destruction.
Descartes was still feeding his authority to THE Primordial Paradox and Erwin. The old philosopher kept them anchored in a state of simultaneous life and death.
Noah analyzed the old man. He had fought beside him, yet he had never truly quantified him.
He activated THE Protagonist’s Omniscient Regard again as this time, there should be no question marks.
WAA!
|Descartes|
|VERITAS: 85|
|PROVENANCE: 0|
|POTENTIA: 65|
|PONDUS: 60|

Noah processed the numbers. The old philosopher possessed a Trueness of eighty-five. It vastly exceeded all of his other attributes. This meant his fundamental identity was so rigidly defined that existence had a remarkably difficult time arguing with his logic. He was a being constructed entirely of undeniable certainty.
Noah floated over the sea of blood. His stellar blue-gold body stopped a few feet away from the philosopher.

"You possess a Trueness that exceeds my own. Who are you really, Descartes? Do you truly plan to go against Those Who Remain? And what are your aims for the two paradoxes you have claimed as disciples?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5674: Movement II
paragraphs: Descartes did not break his concentration on the two flickering figures. He kept his hands raised, his unfathomable eyes fixed on the immediate space before him.
"I...used to be a caretaker of a Lineage of Provenance Lifeforms,"Descartes replied.
"I saw firsthand how Those Who Remain could be when such beings ever sent a wisp of their aura down into the lower realities. It is a crushing, absolute weight."
The old philosopher lowered his hands slightly as the flickering of the two students finally stabilized.

"I know how impossible a rebellion is. I was only a caretaker. But the lowliest things always stand the chance of being the strongest. Erwin here was only a peasant, and look at him now. He drew me the most as his master was also proficient in paradox. Under my guidance, I actually plan to have them become extremely sharp swords of paradox. We will use them to cut across much of what is coming with me."
Noah looked at Descartes silently. He gauged the words.
A caretaker raising swords. It was an act of extreme, calculated defiance. He looked at the two paradoxes recovering on the rusted ground. They were biological weapons being forged in real time!
Noah nodded.

"Existence is vast, and we all have our moving parts," Noah said calmly. "Your words inadvertently allowed me to arrive at an epiphany earlier. Existence is give and take. Do you want anything from me?"
Descartes fell entirely silent. He looked at the ruined sky of the Dimensional Cabin. He calculated the weight of his own request against the capability of THE True Human Emperor.
He eventually lowered his gaze.
"Could you bring me a corpse of a Provenance Lifeform in the next few days, months, or years?"Descartes asked quietly."I have use for it, but I know the ask is a heavy one."
BOOM!
The request struck the air with massive conceptual weight!
Why would a philosopher want the corpse of a Sovereign?
It was a highly logical request, even if the procurement of such an item was statistically impossible for nearly any other being.
"A few days will likely be sufficient," Noah replied, his tone perfectly even. "Are you heading up or down?"
He asked Descartes if they would move toward the front or the back of THE Dimensional Provenance Train.

"We will go down," Descartes answered smoothly. "Our power can paradoxically rise whether we go up or down. But down is a bit more manageable. It was the reason why we came down into this Dimensional Cabin in the first place."
Noah nodded.
"Then I will find you again to give it to you,"Noah stated. "It seems we must rush out of here before any dogs start sniffing."
Descartes nodded calmly. He stepped back, allowing his two disciples to stand.
Noah looked at THE Primordial Paradox. He extended his glowing blue-gold hand.
The boisterous anomaly stepped forward and met the gesture, and the physical collision of their palms occurred.

Noah analyzed the kinetic transfer. It was a localized human greeting. Previously, he had felt the weight of camaraderie and shared battle during this gesture. Now, he observed the collision of atoms and the social programming of a primate species. It felt entirely different..but as a human, he still felt good having something that could be called friendship!
THE Primordial Paradox seemed to have also sensed this change as he smiled lightly.
Noah lowered his hand and turned his endlessly blue eyes toward Erwin.

"You are unique, even with our past history,"Noah said to THE Living Paradox. "Information is paramount in existence, and you are THE Information Paradox. You have the potential to be grand. That is only if you make the right moves. Good luck."
Erwin nodded slowly, his eyes wide as he looked at the terrifying, blurring figure of the True Human Emperor.
Noah did not wait for a response.

He turned his back on the three of them and began to float upward, moving toward the distant, shattered doorway in the sky that led out of THE Serenaros Dimension, towards the forward sections of THE Dimensional Provenance Train!
He looked down at the far corner of the ruined blood-sea. Mahishasura was still kneeling on a floating chunk of rusted metal, bleeding and utterly subdued.
He would be leaving Mahishasura as a biological sensor. This Descendant would remain behind as a tool just to see what arrives here!
Noah reached the upper boundaries of the sky. He did not take an army with him as he took only the massive, hovering Dream Construct of THE Sundered Scion that floated obediently behind his shoulder.
He pushed through the torn fabric of the sky and stepped out into the crushing dark.
<Vasiliou Elseworld>
Across the continuum, in a hidden Warren where THE Argent Loom barely reached, his other body was arriving somewhere far more interesting.
The storm of ancient golden light released them.
Noah’s feet settled onto a road of fused white gold, and he looked up, and he began to see wonder.
A city climbed the sky in front of him.

It rose in concentric tiers from a wide golden plain, seven ringed levels stacked one atop the other against the face of a white prominence, each tier walled, each wall gated, each gate offset from the one below it so that no straight line ran from the ground to the summit.
Towers stood along the ring-walls in unhurried intervals.

At the crown of the highest tier, a fortress of massive drum towers and long halls sat heavy and red-gold in the light, its roofs steep, its windows tall and dark, a seat built by beings who understood that the appearance of patience was itself a weapon.
And behind the city, a mountain floated.
It hung in the sky with no chain and no foundation, a golden mountain the size of an Observable Existence!

Power poured off its slopes in slow, continuous falls of stellar blue-gold essence, sheets of it descending for miles before thinning into the air, feeding the plain, feeding the city, feeding the light itself.
The pressure of it reached across the whole valley and pressed gently and endlessly on everything below.
Noah processed the architecture with detached precision.
The city was a fortress, and that was the first anomaly. A Provenance Lifeform generated its own standing and owed nothing to siege or scarcity.
A civilization of such beings did not need ringed walls and offset gates. Walls, for them, were either memory or message.

Either this lineage had once been besieged badly enough to build in stone what they no longer trusted to sovereignty, or the entire city was a statement aimed outward at visitors, a sentence written in fortifications.
It was...showy.
The second anomaly was the count.
His perception swept the tiers, and lifeforms answered it by the thousands.
Thousands.
Signatures burned across every level of the city, moving along the ring-roads, gathered in the courtyards, seated in the long halls, and each one of them was a one with a Provenance!
Not soldiers drawing on a master’s power.
Every single signature generated itself, a self-sustaining sun in miniature, and there were thousands of them arranged in tiers up a mountainside.
He had met three Provenance Lifeforms in his entire existence. Thalia. Rosalia. The scraps of a voice within THE Aurate Collar.
He had reasoned from that scarcity that the species was small in number!
He revised the model without sentiment.
A voice arrived directly inside his mind at this time!

’Welcome to Vasileia, my Provenance. The Elsecity of my lineage. Every Provenance Lifeform of the Vasiliou line that still exists is somewhere on those tiers right now, and some of them are about to have very strong opinions about you.’
She stood beside him, her hand finding his, and the mental message continued with an edge of dry affection.

’I know how you can be. A bit hard headed. More than a bit tyrannical. You look at a room full of ancient beings and you begin thinking which of them to offend first. So let me take the lead here, just at the start. You defend your women, I know. But I can defend myself. And I can also defend you.’
